output.title: Empire, Defeat and the Search for a New China
output.about: How Japan rebuilt after imperial defeat, while China searched for sovereignty, equality and a workable republic.

chapters.title: Modern Against the West
chapters.narration: पहला chapter। Modern होकर West के खिलाफ कैसे खड़े हों?

beats.say: पिछली बार Japan के नए homes, industries और cultural freedom के साथ बढ़ती military power देखी थी। अब उसी tension से आगे बढ़ते हैं: देश को powerful बनाना और उसके लोगों की ज़िंदगी बेहतर बनाना, क्या हमेशा एक ही बात है?
beats.show: Central question: Does national power mean a better life?

beats.say: आज Japan में empire, defeat और rebuilding से चलकर China में reform और republic तक पहुँचेंगे। दोनों जगह लोगों की तलाश है national strength की, लेकिन सवाल है कि उस strength में ordinary लोगों के लिए क्या जगह होगी।
beats.show: Story arc: Empire → Defeat → Rebuilding | Reform → Republic

beats.say: 1930s और 1940s में Japan का state-centred nationalism अपने सबसे आक्रामक रूप में सामने आया। Nation के नाम पर state की ताकत और उसके goals को सबसे ऊपर रखा जाने लगा।
beats.show: State-centred nationalism: State goals placed above dissent

beats.say: Map पर China और बाकी Asia की तरफ Japan के expansion को देखिए। Empire बढ़ाने के लिए शुरू हुई इन लड़ाइयों का conflict, USA के Pearl Harbor पर Japanese attack के बाद Second World War के बड़े संघर्ष में जुड़ गया।
beats.show: Map: Japan, China, Southeast Asia and Pearl Harbor

beats.say: बाहर war बढ़ी, तो अंदर society पर controls भी बढ़े। Dissidents, यानी government से असहमति रखने वाले लोग, repression और imprisonment का सामना कर रहे थे।
beats.show: War abroad; tighter control at home

beats.say: War के support में patriotic societies बनीं, और इनमें कई women's organisations भी थीं। पिछली बार women workers और modern girl देखी थीं; अब महिलाओं की public participation का एक और रूप है, state के war project में mobilisation।
beats.show: Patriotic societies and women's wartime mobilisation

beats.say: लेकिन यहाँ एक intellectual problem थी। Japan ने modern science और institutions से अपनी ताकत बनाई थी; अब उसी West से लड़ते हुए modern कैसे बना रहे?
beats.show: The dilemma: Use modernity while fighting the West

beats.say: किताब 1943 के एक influential symposium को इसी नाम से रखती है, Overcoming Modernity। Symposium मतलब ऐसा organised discussion, जहाँ अलग-अलग fields के लोग एक बड़े सवाल पर अपने ideas रखते हैं।
beats.show: Overcoming Modernity: An intellectual symposium

beats.say: Musician Moroi Saburo ने music के बारे में पूछा: क्या उसका काम केवल senses को excite करना है, या उसे spirit की art फिर बनाया जा सकता है? मतलब केवल कानों को अच्छा लगना नहीं, अंदर की सोच और अनुभव को भी छूना।
beats.show: Moroi Saburo: Sensory stimulation or an art of the spirit?

beats.say: क्या वह Western music को पूरी तरह फेंक देना चाहते थे? नहीं, वह सिर्फ Japanese धुन को Western instruments पर बजा देने से आगे का रास्ता खोज रहे थे।
beats.show: Not rejection; not imitation; a new musical vision

beats.say: अब philosopher Nishitani Keiji आए। उनके लिए modern, Western thought की तीन streams का मेल था: Renaissance, Protestant Reformation और natural sciences का rise।
beats.show: Nishitani: Renaissance + Protestant Reformation + Natural sciences

beats.say: Renaissance में learning और human creativity को नया ज़ोर मिला; Protestant Reformation ने Western Christianity की authority और practices को challenge किया। Natural sciences ने nature को समझने के लिए observation और investigation की ताकत बढ़ाई।
beats.show: Three streams: Learning | Religious reform | Scientific inquiry

beats.say: Nishitani ने कहा कि Japan की moral energy ने उसे colony बनने से बचाया था। Moral energy का यह term उन्होंने German philosopher Ranke से लिया था।
beats.show: Moral energy: A term borrowed from Ranke

beats.say: उनके मुताबिक अब Japan का duty था एक नया world order, Greater East Asia, बनाना। इसके लिए science और religion को एक vision में जोड़ना ज़रूरी था।
beats.show: Nishitani's proposal: Greater East Asia; science with religion

beats.say: यहाँ सावधानी रखिए: यह उनके विचार थे, empire की निष्पक्ष सच्चाई नहीं। Asia को नया order देने का दावा, दूसरे Asian लोगों पर Japanese control को सही ठहराने में भी इस्तेमाल हो सकता था।
beats.show: Claim versus consequence: Liberation or imperial control?

beats.say: अब किताब का सवाल लीजिए: क्या आप Nishitani की modern की definition से agree करेंगे? पहले सोचिए, क्या किसी society का modern होना केवल उसके ideas की European ancestry से तय हो जाएगा?
beats.show: Activity 2: Do you agree with Nishitani's definition of modern?

beats.say: उनकी definition useful है, क्योंकि वह modern Western thought की important roots पहचानती है। लेकिन पूरी नहीं है: industry, capitalism, nation-states, citizenship और political rights भी modern life को shape करते हैं।
beats.show: Useful intellectual roots, but not a complete definition

beats.say: और Japan जैसे societies इन ideas को बस copy नहीं करते, अपनी conditions में बदलते भी हैं। इसलिए definition से कुछ सीख सकते हैं, पर उससे Japan के empire बनाने को कोई moral permission नहीं मिल जाती।
beats.show: Modernity is adapted locally; it does not justify empire

chapters.title: Defeat and a Different State
chapters.narration: दूसरा chapter। Defeat के बाद state को नया रूप मिलता है।

beats.say: Japan का colonial empire बनाने का project Allied forces के हाथों defeat पर खत्म हुआ। Hiroshima और Nagasaki पर गिराए गए atomic bombs ने immense destruction और suffering पैदा की।
beats.show: Map: Hiroshima and Nagasaki; imperial defeat

beats.say: इन bombs के इस्तेमाल पर दो interpretations हैं। एक argument है कि इनसे war छोटी हुई; दूसरे लोग कहते हैं कि इतना विनाश और suffering unnecessary थी।
beats.show: Atomic bomb debate: Shorten the war? Unnecessary suffering?

beats.say: दोनों arguments का मौजूद होना समझिए, लेकिन suffering को debate के पीछे गायब मत होने दीजिए। National power की हमारी कहानी का यहाँ बहुत भारी human cost सामने आता है।
beats.show: The human cost of imperial war

beats.say: Defeat के बाद US-led Occupation में Japan को demilitarise किया गया और नया constitution आया। किताब इस शुरुआती reform phase को 1945 से 1947 के साथ रखती है; पूरी Occupation 1945 से 1952 तक चली थी।
beats.show: US-led Occupation: 1945–1952 | Early constitutional reforms: 1945–1947

beats.say: अब सोचिए, जिस state ने war को expansion का रास्ता बनाया था, उसके नए constitution में सबसे साफ बदलाव क्या हो सकता था? Article 9, जिसे no war clause कहते हैं।
beats.show: Article 9: The no-war clause

beats.say: इस clause ने war को state policy के instrument की तरह इस्तेमाल करना renounce किया। मतलब देश के political goals पूरे करने के लिए war को अपना रास्ता न मानना।
beats.show: War renounced as an instrument of state policy

beats.say: बदलाव केवल army तक नहीं रुका। Agrarian reforms हुए, trade unions फिर स्थापित हुईं और economy पर हावी बड़े monopoly houses, zaibatsu, को dismantle करने की कोशिश हुई।
beats.show: Reforms: Land | Trade unions | Monopoly business houses

beats.say: Zaibatsu पिछली lecture वाले family-controlled business groups हैं। यहाँ कोशिश शब्द important है; कोई policy घोषित हो जाने से उसका हर goal पूरा हो गया, ऐसा नहीं मानना चाहिए।
beats.show: Policy aim is not the same as complete implementation

beats.say: Political parties revive हुईं और 1946 में पहली post-war elections हुईं। इनमें Japanese women ने पहली बार vote दिया।
beats.show: 1946 elections: Women vote for the first time

beats.say: तो एक बड़ा shift देखिए: national strength का मतलब अब केवल army और empire नहीं रह गया। Political participation और organised labour के लिए भी जगह खुल रही थी।
beats.show: From imperial mobilisation toward wider political participation

beats.say: इसके बाद economy की rapid rebuilding को post-war miracle कहा गया। लेकिन miracle बोलते ही क्या हम उसकी असली वजहें समझ लेते हैं?
beats.show: The post-war miracle: What explains it?

beats.say: नहीं, Japan का लंबा history इसके पीछे काम कर रहा था। Popular struggles और political participation बढ़ाने पर intellectual debates पहले से थीं; constitution अब democratise हुआ, उसकी माँग की जड़ें पुरानी थीं।
beats.show: Historical roots: Popular struggles and intellectual debate

beats.say: Pre-war social cohesion भी मजबूत हुई, जिससे government, bureaucracy और industry करीब से मिलकर काम कर सके। पुरानी organisational strengths को अब rebuilding में लगाया गया।
beats.show: Close coordination: Government ↔ Bureaucracy ↔ Industry

beats.say: US support ने मदद की, और Korean तथा Vietnamese wars से पैदा हुई demand ने Japanese economy को भी फायदा पहुँचाया। यह uncomfortable connection है: एक country's rebuilding को दूसरे इलाकों की wars से economic demand मिल रही थी।
beats.show: External support and demand from the Korean and Vietnamese wars

beats.say: 1964 के Tokyo Olympics इस comeback के symbolic coming of age बने। दुनिया के सामने Japan अपनी नई economic और organisational capacity दिखा रहा था।
beats.show: 1964 Tokyo Olympics: A symbol of renewed standing

beats.say: उसी साल Shinkansen, यानी bullet-train network, शुरू हुआ। तेज़ trains Japan की advanced technology से better और cheaper goods बनाने की क्षमता का symbol बन गईं।
beats.show: 1964: Shinkansen begins; technology becomes a national symbol

beats.say: Speed के numbers पर एक correction ज़रूरी है। किताब शुरुआत के लिए 200 miles per hour और बाद के लिए 300 miles per hour लिखती है, लेकिन इन units को reliable service speeds न मानिए।
beats.show: Unit warning: The textbook's 200 and 300 mph figures are inaccurate

beats.say: 1964 की शुरुआती Shinkansen service की top speed करीब 210 kilometre per hour थी; बाद की कई services करीब 300 kilometre per hour या उससे ऊपर चलीं। Main historical point है high-speed transport का विकास, गलत unit याद करना नहीं।
beats.show: Correct scale: About 210 km/h initially; later services around 300 km/h and above

chapters.title: Whose Miracle?
chapters.narration: तीसरा chapter। Economic miracle की कीमत कौन चुका रहा था?

beats.say: Tokyo की ये before-and-after तस्वीरें साथ देखिए। पुरानी street में हाथ से खींचा जाने वाला rickshaw, शुरुआती motor vehicles और अलग-अलग तरह के कपड़े पहने pedestrians साथ हैं।
beats.show: Tokyo before the war: Rickshaw, early cars and pedestrians

beats.say: दूसरी तस्वीर में broad road, cars, bus और घनी commercial buildings दिखती हैं। यह urban transformation का evidence है, लेकिन photograph अकेली हमें wages, health या political freedom नहीं बता सकती।
beats.show: Tokyo after the war: Motor traffic and dense commercial development

beats.say: अब मान लीजिए factory का output बढ़ रहा है, लेकिन आसपास का पानी जहरीला हो रहा है। क्या output की बढ़ोतरी को ही पूरी success कह देंगे?
beats.show: Higher output + poisoned water: Is growth enough?

beats.say: 1960s में Japan में civil society movements बढ़ीं, क्योंकि industrialisation में health और environment के effects की बहुत अनदेखी हुई थी। Civil society यहाँ state के बाहर लोगों के organised public efforts हैं।
beats.show: Civil society: Organised public action outside the state

beats.say: पहले cadmium poisoning से होने वाली painful disease ने खतरे का संकेत दिया। फिर 1960s में Minamata में mercury poisoning, और early 1970s में air pollution की problems सामने आईं।
beats.show: Pollution warnings: Cadmium → Minamata mercury → Air pollution

beats.say: Cadmium और mercury दोनों toxic metals हैं; इसलिए problem केवल गंदा दिखने वाला पानी नहीं थी। Industrial pollution लोगों की bodies और रोज़ की ज़िंदगी में घुस रहा था।
beats.show: Industrial pollution becomes a public-health crisis

beats.say: Grass-roots pressure groups ने कहा कि इन problems को officially recognise करो और victims को compensation दो। Grass-roots मतलब शुरुआत सीधे affected लोगों और local communities से होना।
beats.show: Community demands: Recognition and compensation

beats.say: Government action और नए legal regulations से conditions सुधरीं। याद है Tanaka Shozo की earlier struggle? अब उसी तरह ordinary लोगों के दबाव ने industrial progress की शर्तों को फिर challenge किया।
beats.show: Public pressure → Government action → Environmental regulation

beats.say: Japan ने दुनिया के कुछ strictest environmental controls बनाए। किताब बताती है कि mid-1980s से environmental issues में public interest घटने लगा, लेकिन इसका मतलब हर environmental problem खत्म होना नहीं है।
beats.show: Strict controls; declining public interest from the mid-1980s

beats.say: एक developed country के रूप में Japan के सामने challenge रहा कि अपनी political और technological capabilities से leading world power की position कैसे बनाए रखे। मगर अब हमारे पास power को परखने के लिए health और public voice के सवाल भी हैं।
beats.show: A developed nation's challenge: Leadership, technology and public welfare

beats.say: यहीं book के essay question को पकड़ते हैं: क्या rapid industrialisation ने Japan को neighbours से wars और environmental destruction की तरफ धकेला? जवाब में connection दिखाना है, लेकिन industrialisation को अकेला कारण नहीं बनाना।
beats.show: Essay question 6: Industrialisation, war and environmental destruction

beats.say: Industries ने resources और military capacity की demand बढ़ाई; state-centred nationalism और military की independent power ने उस capacity को imperial expansion में लगाया। Western domination का डर भी expansion और opposition दबाने का justification बना।
beats.show: War: Industrial capacity + militarism + imperial ambition + fear

beats.say: Environment में unregulated growth, natural resources की demand और pollution ने खेतों, पानी, हवा और health को नुकसान पहुँचाया। Ashio से Minamata तक evidence है, लेकिन protest और regulation यह भी दिखाते हैं कि destruction कोई unavoidable destiny नहीं था।
beats.show: Environment: Unregulated growth → Damage; protest → Regulation

chapters.title: China and the Silver Triangle
chapters.narration: चौथा chapter। China में trade का सवाल sovereignty का संकट बनता है।

beats.say: अब समुद्र के पार China की तरफ आते हैं। Japan की तरह यहाँ भी national strength का सवाल था, लेकिन उसके साथ sovereignty वापस पाने, foreign occupation का humiliation खत्म करने और equality तथा development लाने की चुनौती थी।
beats.show: China's challenge: Sovereignty, dignity, equality and development

beats.say: Sovereignty मतलब अपने देश के फैसलों पर अपना अंतिम control। Flag अपना हो, लेकिन resources और decisions पर foreign powers हावी हों, तो sovereignty का सवाल फिर भी उठता है।
beats.show: Sovereignty: Final authority over a country's own affairs

beats.say: Chinese debates में तीन broad responses दिखे। पहले reformers Kang Youwei, जो 1858 से 1927 तक रहे, और Liang Qichao, जिनका जीवन 1873 से 1929 तक था।
beats.show: Reformers: Kang Youwei (1858–1927); Liang Qichao (1873–1929)

beats.say: ये traditional ideas को नए तरीके से इस्तेमाल करके West के challenge का सामना करना चाहते थे। दूसरा रास्ता Sun Yat-sen जैसे republican revolutionaries का था, जो Japan और West के ideas से inspiration लेते थे।
beats.show: Reform tradition, or replace monarchy with a republic?

beats.say: तीसरा response Communist Party of China, यानी CCP, का था: foreigners को हटाओ और बहुत पुरानी inequalities भी खत्म करो। अभी इन तीन रास्तों को पहचानिए; CCP की पूरी कहानी अगली lecture में खोलेंगे।
beats.show: Three paths: Reformers | Republicans | Communists

beats.say: China का modern West से contact सीधे nineteenth-century war से शुरू नहीं हुआ था। Sixteenth और seventeenth centuries में Jesuit missionaries astronomy और mathematics जैसी Western sciences लाए थे।
beats.show: Sixteenth–seventeenth centuries: Jesuit science contacts

beats.say: उनका immediate impact limited था, लेकिन contacts का सिलसिला शुरू हुआ। Nineteenth century में यह रिश्ता बिल्कुल अलग और violent direction में बढ़ा, जब Britain ने profitable opium trade फैलाने के लिए force इस्तेमाल की।
beats.show: From scientific contact to coercive trade expansion

beats.say: Opium War क्यों हुई, यह समझने के लिए पहले एक tea cup पकड़िए, imagine कीजिए। Britain में Chinese tea, silk और porcelain की demand थी, मगर Chinese buyers उतना Western सामान नहीं खरीद रहे थे।
beats.show: British demand: Tea, silk and porcelain

beats.say: तो payment कैसे हो? Silver से; और जब खरीद बहुत ज़्यादा हो, बिक्री कम, तो silver बाहर जाता रहेगा। यही Britain की तरफ से balance-of-trade problem थी।
beats.show: Trade imbalance: Chinese goods to Britain; silver to China

beats.say: East India Company को इसका एक खतरनाक रास्ता मिला, India में उगाई जाने वाली opium। इस network में opium China में बेची गई और उससे silver कमाया गया।
beats.show: Map triangle: Indian opium → China

beats.say: Opium बेचने वाले यह silver Canton में Company agents को देते और बदले में letters of credit लेते थे। Letter of credit को आसान भाषा में समझिए, दूसरे स्थान पर payment लेने का documented credit claim।
beats.show: Canton: Silver deposited → Letters of credit received

beats.say: Company उसी silver से Chinese tea, silk और porcelain खरीदकर Britain में बेचती थी। Map पर पूरा triangle बन गया: Britain, India और China के बीच triangular trade।
beats.show: Britain–India–China: Opium, silver, Chinese goods and credit

beats.say: इसलिए इसे केवल दो देशों के बीच चीज़ों की अदला-बदली मत मानिए। Colonial India की production और China में opium की बिक्री, British trade को finance करने के लिए जुड़ी हुई थीं।
beats.show: Colonial production linked to international trade finance

beats.say: British force के इस्तेमाल से first Opium War हुई, 1839 से 1842 के बीच। इससे ruling Qing dynasty कमजोर हुई और reform तथा change की माँग मजबूत हुई।
beats.show: First Opium War, 1839–1842: Qing authority weakened

beats.say: अब European painting में centre की burning ship और ऊपर उठता smoke देखिए। Chinese junks की चौड़ी ribbed sails, दूर European-style warships, छोटी boats और floating wreckage, ये war की violence दिखाते हैं।
beats.show: Opium War painting: Burning vessel, junks and wreckage

beats.say: किताब पूछती है: क्या यह painting Opium War की significance का clear sense देती है? अपनी नज़र से पहले जवाब बनाइए, क्या दिख रहा है और क्या नहीं?
beats.show: Activity 3: Does the painting explain the war's significance?

beats.say: यह destruction और naval conflict को बहुत साफ महसूस कराती है। लेकिन opium trade का triangle, British commercial interests और Qing authority पर लंबे असर को painting अकेली नहीं समझाती।
beats.show: Visible: Destruction | Missing: Trade causes and political consequences

beats.say: और यह European representation है, किसी camera की neutral recording नहीं। इसलिए picture useful source है, पूरी explanation नहीं; उसे trade और political context के साथ पढ़ना होगा।
beats.show: Read the image with its viewpoint and historical context

chapters.title: Changing the Gatekeepers
chapters.narration: पाँचवाँ chapter। China को बचाने के लिए पुरानी व्यवस्था कितनी बदलनी होगी?

beats.say: Kang Youwei और Liang Qichao जैसे Qing reformers का जवाब था, system को मजबूत और modern बनाओ। Modern administration, नई army और education system के साथ constitutional government की तरफ local assemblies बनाने की policies आईं।
beats.show: Qing reform agenda: Administration, army, education and local assemblies

beats.say: Goal था China को colonisation से बचाना। लेकिन किसी खतरे को समझाने के लिए लोग अक्सर दूसरे देश का example देते हैं; Chinese thinkers ने Poland और India की तरफ देखा।
beats.show: Warnings from abroad: Poland and India

beats.say: Eighteenth century में Poland का partition इतना चर्चित example बना कि late 1890s में Chinese में एक phrase चलने लगी, bolan wo, यानी हमें Poland बना देना। मतलब देश को बाहरी ताकतें बाँट दें।
beats.show: Partition of Poland → bolan wo: To partition us like Poland

beats.say: 1903 में Liang Qichao ने India के बारे में लिखा कि एक country को एक non-country, East India Company, ने खत्म कर दिया। उनका point था कि national awareness के बिना कोई society foreign domination का मुकाबला कैसे करेगी?
beats.show: Liang, 1903: A country defeated by a company

beats.say: उन्होंने Indians को अपने लोगों के प्रति cruel और British के सामने subservient बताकर criticise किया। इसे उनका judgment समझिए, Indians के बारे में हमारा final verdict नहीं।
beats.show: A reformer's argument, not a neutral verdict on Indians

beats.say: उनके argument का appeal इसलिए भी था कि ordinary Chinese, China के खिलाफ British wars में Indian soldiers को देख सकते थे। Colonial rule में एक society के resources और soldiers दूसरी society को दबाने में इस्तेमाल हो सकते थे।
beats.show: British wars in China used Indian soldiers

beats.say: लेकिन क्या नई army बना देने से सोचने का पुराना ढाँचा अपने-आप बदल जाएगा? कई Chinese thinkers को लगा कि traditional ways of thinking को भी बदलना होगा।
beats.show: Institutional reform also raises questions about inherited ideas

beats.say: यहाँ बड़ा नाम है Confucianism, जो Confucius और उनके disciples की teachings से विकसित हुआ। Confucius 551 से 479 BCE के बीच रहे।
beats.show: Confucianism: Confucius (551–479 BCE) and his disciples

beats.say: इसमें good conduct, practical wisdom और proper social relationships पर ज़ोर था। इसने life के प्रति Chinese attitudes, social standards और political theories तथा institutions को गहराई से shape किया।
beats.show: Conduct, practical wisdom and social relationships

beats.say: अब बहुत-से reform-minded लोग इसे नए ideas और institutions के रास्ते की बड़ी barrier समझने लगे। ध्यान रखिए, यह उस समय का critical reassessment था; tradition हमेशा से सबको बेकार लगती थी, ऐसा नहीं।
beats.show: An influential tradition is re-evaluated as a barrier

beats.say: Modern subjects सीखने के लिए students Japan, Britain और France भेजे गए। 1890s में बहुत-से Chinese students Japan पहुँचे, और उनमें कई आगे leading republicans बने।
beats.show: Map: Chinese students travel to Japan, Britain and France

beats.say: एक interesting reversal देखिए। कभी Japan ने China से बहुत knowledge लिया था; अब Chinese लोग justice, rights और revolution जैसे European concepts के Japanese translations तक उधार ले रहे थे।
beats.show: A reversal of knowledge flows: Japan → China

beats.say: Shared Chinese-character writing tradition ने इसमें मदद की। Spoken languages अलग होने के बावजूद, characters में लिखे नए terms Chinese readers के लिए अपनाना आसान था।
beats.show: Shared characters help new political vocabulary travel

beats.say: 1905 में, Russo-Japanese War के तुरंत बाद, centuries-old Chinese examination system खत्म किया गया। वह war Chinese soil पर और Chinese territory को लेकर लड़ी गई थी, इसलिए China की कमजोरी और भी साफ थी।
beats.show: 1905: Examination system abolished after the Russo-Japanese War

beats.say: इस exam की importance समझने के लिए imagine कीजिए कि पूरे ruling elite का मुख्य entry gate एक exam हो। China में 1850 तक करीब ग्यारह लाख की elite ruling class में entry का बड़ा रास्ता यही था।
beats.show: Elite entry gate: Examinations | Ruling elite: About 1.1 million

beats.say: Candidate को classical Chinese में एक prescribed form का eight-legged essay लिखना पड़ता था, जिसे pa-ku wen कहते थे। Eight-legged का मतलब यहाँ तय structure है, कोई आठ पैरों वाली writing नहीं!
beats.show: Pa-ku wen: The prescribed eight-legged essay

beats.say: अलग-अलग levels पर यह examination हर तीन साल में दो बार held होता था। बैठने की permission पाने वालों में भी first level पर केवल 1 से 2 per cent pass करते थे।
beats.show: Frequency: Twice every three years | First-level pass rate: 1–2%

beats.say: आम तौर पर करीब 24 साल की उम्र तक first level pass करने वाला beautiful talent कहलाता था। Imagine कीजिए, सौ eligible candidates में सिर्फ एक या दो को यह शुरुआती success मिले।
beats.show: First-level success: Beautiful talent, usually around age 24

beats.say: 1850 से पहले किसी समय पूरे देश में करीब 5,26,869 civil और 2,12,330 military provincial degree holders होते थे। इन degree holders को sheng-yuan कहते थे।
beats.show: Sheng-yuan: 526,869 civil and 212,330 military degree holders

beats.say: लेकिन official positions केवल 27,000 थीं। तो degree मिलना भी job की guarantee नहीं था; बहुत-से lower-level degree holders बिना सरकारी jobs के रह जाते थे।
beats.show: Only 27,000 official posts: Qualification did not guarantee employment

beats.say: और exam मुख्य रूप से literary skills माँगता था, modern science या technology नहीं। इसी वजह से इसे scientific और technological development की barrier माना गया।
beats.show: Literary selection versus modern scientific and technical skills

beats.say: 1905 में इसे abolish करने का logic था कि classical learning की ये tested skills modern world की ज़रूरतों से मेल नहीं खा रही थीं। अब सवाल केवल किसे चुनें का नहीं था, किस तरह की ability चुनें का था।
beats.show: 1905 reform: Change the skills that earn authority

beats.say: अब brief-answer question लीजिए: Qing dynasty ने Western challenge का सामना करने की क्या कोशिश की? जवाब है administration, army और education को modern बनाना, local assemblies से constitutional government की तरफ जाना और students को modern subjects सीखने विदेश भेजना।
beats.show: Brief question 3: Qing responses to the Western challenge

beats.say: 1905 में old examination system खत्म करना भी इसी बदलाव का हिस्सा था। इन कोशिशों का goal dynasty और China को मजबूत बनाना था, लेकिन बढ़ती revolutionary माँगों को ये रोक नहीं सकीं।
beats.show: Reform did not end the demand for revolutionary change

chapters.title: A Republic Is Not Enough
chapters.narration: छठा chapter। Monarchy हट गई, अब नया China कैसे बनेगा?

beats.say: 1911 की revolution में Manchu empire गिरा और Sun Yat-sen के नेतृत्व में republic का रास्ता खुला, जो formally 1912 में स्थापित हुई। Sun Yat-sen को modern China का founder माना जाता है।
beats.show: 1911 revolution → Republic formally established in 1912

beats.say: Sun 1866 से 1925 तक रहे और एक poor family से आए थे। Missionary schools में उन्हें democracy और Christianity के ideas मिले; उन्होंने medicine पढ़ी, लेकिन China के future की चिंता उन्हें politics की तरफ ले गई।
beats.show: Sun Yat-sen (1866–1925): Medicine, missionary education and national reform

beats.say: उनके programme का नाम था Three Principles, San min chui। इसे किसी ruler को हटाने की एक ही demand मत समझिए; इसमें nation, government और economic life, तीनों के लिए vision था।
beats.show: Three Principles: Nationalism | Democracy | Socialism

beats.say: पहला principle nationalism था: Manchu dynasty को हटाना, जिसे उनके followers foreign dynasty मानते थे, और दूसरे foreign imperialists से भी छुटकारा पाना। यह उनकी nationalist understanding थी।
beats.show: Nationalism: End Manchu rule and foreign imperialism

beats.say: दूसरा democracy, यानी democratic government स्थापित करना। तीसरा socialism था, जिसका यहाँ specific मतलब capital को regulate करना और landholdings को equalise करना था।
beats.show: Democracy: Democratic government | Socialism: Regulate capital, equalise land

beats.say: अब book का चौथा brief question यहीं answer कीजिए: Sun Yat-sen के Three Principles क्या थे? Nationalism से foreign domination खत्म करना, democracy से democratic government और socialism से capital regulation तथा land equality लाना।
beats.show: Brief question 4: Explain all three principles, not just their names

beats.say: लेकिन emperor हट जाने से political और social instability खत्म नहीं हुई। Republic बनाना एक institutional शुरुआत थी, पूरे देश को stable और equal बनाना अभी बाकी था।
beats.show: Republic proclaimed ≠ Stability achieved

beats.say: 4 May 1919 को Beijing में गुस्से से भरा demonstration हुआ। First World War की victorious side, जिसे Britain lead कर रहा था, का ally होने के बाद भी China को उससे छीने गए territories वापस नहीं मिले थे।
beats.show: 4 May 1919, Beijing: Protest against the post-war peace settlement

beats.say: अब बताइए, अगर आप victory वाली side पर हों, फिर भी आपकी territory वापस न हो, तो कैसा लगेगा? इसी humiliation से निकला protest एक बड़े movement में बदल गया।
beats.show: Unequal treatment turns a protest into the May Fourth Movement

beats.say: इसने पूरी generation को tradition challenge करने और modern science, democracy तथा nationalism से China बचाने की तरफ धकेला। Revolutionaries foreigners का resource control खत्म करने के साथ inequalities और poverty हटाना चाहते थे।
beats.show: May Fourth: Science, democracy, nationalism and social reform

beats.say: उनकी demands everyday life तक जाती थीं: writing में simple language इस्तेमाल हो, foot-binding खत्म हो और women की subordination समाप्त हो। Marriage में equality मिले और economic development से poverty कम हो।
beats.show: Reforms: Accessible writing, end foot-binding, women's equality and development

beats.say: Foot-binding में girls के पैरों को कसकर बाँधकर उनकी growth रोकी जाती थी। इसलिए इसे खत्म करने की demand केवल fashion बदलने की बात नहीं, body और freedom पर control को challenge करना था।
beats.show: Foot-binding: Restricting foot growth; a target of reform

beats.say: इस turmoil में दो major forces उभरीं: Guomindang, यानी National People's Party, और CCP। दोनों country को unite करके stability लाना चाहती थीं, लेकिन उनके social programmes और methods अलग होंगे।
beats.show: Two major forces: Guomindang and CCP

beats.say: Sun के ideas Guomindang की political philosophy का आधार बने। Party ने four great needs को सामने रखा: कपड़े, खाना, housing और transportation।
beats.show: Four great needs: Clothing, food, housing and transportation

beats.say: Sun की death के बाद Chiang Kai-shek Guomindang के leader बने। उनका जीवन 1887 से 1975 तक था, और उन्होंने warlords को control करने तथा communists को eliminate करने की military campaign चलाई।
beats.show: Chiang Kai-shek (1887–1975): Campaigns against warlords and communists

beats.say: Warlords वे regional leaders थे जिन्होंने अपने इलाकों में authority अपने हाथ में ले ली थी। उन्हें हराना national unity का सवाल था, लेकिन Chiang का रास्ता nation को militarise भी कर रहा था।
beats.show: Warlords: Regional leaders exercising seized authority

beats.say: Chiang ने secular, rational और this-worldly Confucianism की बात की। मतलब focus इस दुनिया के social conduct पर, लेकिन साथ ही वह लोगों में unified behaviour की habit और instinct पैदा करना चाहते थे।
beats.show: Chiang's vision: Secular Confucianism and disciplined collective behaviour

beats.say: Women के लिए उन्होंने chastity, appearance, speech और work की four virtues पर ज़ोर दिया। उनकी भूमिका household तक सीमित मानी गई, यहाँ तक कि कपड़ों की hemlines की length भी prescribe की गई।
beats.show: Women's prescribed virtues and household roles; regulated hemlines

beats.say: तो contrast पकड़िए: May Fourth की marriage equality और women's freedom की demand एक तरफ है। दूसरी तरफ national order के नाम पर उनके behaviour और कपड़ों तक को control करने का project है।
beats.show: Equality and individual freedom versus prescribed social discipline

chapters.title: The People Outside the Promise
chapters.narration: सातवाँ chapter। National programme से बाहर छूटे लोगों की कहानी।

beats.say: Guomindang का social base मुख्य रूप से urban areas में था। Shanghai जैसे modern growth के centres को map पर देखिए, लेकिन याद रखिए, China की industrial growth अभी slow और limited थी।
beats.show: Map: Shanghai and China's coastal urban centres

beats.say: 1919 तक industrial working class करीब पाँच लाख की हो गई थी। मगर modern industries, जैसे shipbuilding, में काम करने वाले उसका केवल छोटा हिस्सा थे।
beats.show: 1919: About 500,000 industrial workers; few in modern industries

beats.say: Urban population का बड़ा हिस्सा petty urbanites, यानी xiao shimin, कहलाता था, जैसे छोटे traders और shopkeepers। इसलिए city की economy को केवल बड़ी factories से बनी हुई मत देखिए।
beats.show: Xiao shimin: Small traders, shopkeepers and petty urban livelihoods

beats.say: Urban workers की wages बहुत low थीं, खासकर women की। Working hours लंबे और conditions खराब थीं; modern city का मतलब हर worker की comfortable life नहीं था।
beats.show: Urban labour: Low wages, long hours and poor conditions

beats.say: साथ ही individualism बढ़ने से women's rights, family कैसे बने और love तथा romance पर नई discussions होने लगीं। पुराने social roles को लोग अपनी personal choices की नज़र से भी देखने लगे थे।
beats.show: New debates: Individual choice, women's rights, family and romance

beats.say: Schools और universities के फैलाव ने इन changes को support किया। Peking University 1902 में established हुई थी, और journalism भी नए thinking को फैलाने का बड़ा medium बना।
beats.show: Education and journalism: Peking University, 1902

beats.say: Popular magazine Life Weekly के editor Zao Taofen थे, जो 1895 से 1944 तक रहे। Magazine नए ideas के साथ Mahatma Gandhi और Turkey के modernist leader Kemal Ataturk जैसे लोगों से readers को परिचित कराती थी।
beats.show: Life Weekly: Zao Taofen (1895–1944); Gandhi and Ataturk

beats.say: इसकी circulation 1926 की केवल 2,000 copies से बढ़कर 1933 में दो लाख copies हो गई। यानी सौ गुना; नए ideas के लिए audience कितनी तेज़ी से बढ़ रही थी, यह उससे दिखाई देता है।
beats.show: Life Weekly circulation: 2,000 in 1926 → 200,000 in 1933

beats.say: लेकिन ideas और magazines के बीच ordinary people's hardship को भी सुनना होगा। 1935 के Shanghai में Black American trumpet player Buck Clayton अपने jazz orchestra के साथ रह रहे थे।
beats.show: Shanghai, 1935: Buck Clayton and his jazz orchestra

beats.say: Expatriate होने के कारण उनकी life में privileges थे, लेकिन Black होने की वजह से racial discrimination भी था। कुछ white Americans ने उन्हें और orchestra members को assault किया और जिस hotel में वे बजाते थे, वहाँ से निकाल दिया।
beats.show: Expatriate privilege alongside racial discrimination

beats.say: खुद discrimination झेलने के कारण Clayton को Chinese लोगों की situation के लिए ज़्यादा sympathy थी। Nationality से वह American थे, लेकिन racial inequality का experience उन्हें दूसरे दबाए गए लोगों से जोड़ रहा था।
beats.show: Shared discrimination can create solidarity across nationalities

beats.say: White Americans के साथ एक fight में जीतने के बाद, Clayton बताते हैं कि Chinese onlookers उनके पीछे घर तक cheers करते गए। जैसे कोई winning football team लौट रही हो, उन्हें लगा कि इन musicians ने वह कर दिया जो वे खुद करना चाहते थे।
beats.show: Chinese onlookers cheer the orchestra's resistance

beats.say: यहीं activity का सवाल है: discrimination का एहसास लोगों को कैसे unite करता है? क्या सिर्फ एक ही देश या community के लोग एक-दूसरे का humiliation समझ सकते हैं?
beats.show: Activity 4: How does a sense of discrimination unite people?

beats.say: नहीं, अपना humiliation दूसरे का humiliation पहचानने में मदद कर सकता है। Shared unfairness से sympathy, common anger और solidarity बन सकती है, जैसा Clayton और Chinese onlookers के बीच दिखाई देता है।
beats.show: Shared unfairness → Recognition → Sympathy → Solidarity

beats.say: लेकिन यह automatic rule नहीं कि discrimination झेलने वाला हर व्यक्ति सबके साथ खड़ा ही होगा। इस example में हमें specific evidence मिलता है कि racial discrimination ने national boundaries के पार connection बनाया।
beats.show: A historical example of solidarity, not an automatic universal rule

beats.say: Clayton ने poverty का एक और scene दर्ज किया। कभी 20 या 30 labourers एक भारी cart खींचते थे, जो America में truck या horses खींचते।
beats.show: Clayton's account: 20–30 labourers pulling a heavy cart

beats.say: दिन के अंत में उन्हें बस दो bowls rice और सोने की जगह भर मिलती थी। Clayton का human horses वाला comparison उस labour की physical hardship पर shock जताता है, लोगों की dignity कम करने के लिए हमारा label नहीं है।
beats.show: A day's labour for a couple of bowls of rice and shelter

beats.say: अब Lan Jia का woodcut Rickshaw Puller देखिए। आगे झुका torso, strained face और shafts पकड़े हाथ, sharp black-and-white lines physical effort को बहुत तीखा बनाती हैं।
beats.show: Lan Jia's Rickshaw Puller: Strain, grip and bodily effort

beats.say: Lao She का 1936 का novel Rickshaw भी classic बना। Literature और visual art, दोनों उन लोगों की ज़िंदगी सामने ला रहे थे जिन्हें national progress के बड़े speeches आसानी से पीछे छोड़ सकते थे।
beats.show: Lao She, Rickshaw, 1936: Literature and urban hardship

beats.say: यही Guomindang की कमजोरी की तरफ ले जाता है। Country unite करने की कोशिश के बावजूद उसका social base narrow और political vision limited रहा।
beats.show: Guomindang's weakness: Narrow base and limited vision

beats.say: Sun के programme में capital regulation और equal landholdings central थे, लेकिन ये लागू नहीं किए गए। Party ने peasantry और बढ़ती social inequalities की अनदेखी की।
beats.show: Unfulfilled promises: Regulating capital and equalising land

beats.say: लोगों की problems address करने के बजाय military order impose करना उसका रास्ता बना। तो nation को disciplined बना देना और उसके लोगों की needs पूरी करना, फिर अलग-अलग बातें निकलीं।
beats.show: Military order without addressing social problems

beats.say: अंत में rising prices वाला visual पढ़िए। एक ही purchasing power से मिलने वाली चीज़ें छोटी होती जाती हैं: 1937 में oxen, 1939 में pig और 1941 में flour का sack।
beats.show: Falling purchasing power: Oxen, 1937 → Pig, 1939 → Flour, 1941

beats.say: आगे 1943 में hen, 1945 में eggs, 1947 में coal का piece और 1949 में paper की sheet है। यहाँ कोई exact cash amount नहीं दिया है; picture का point है money की buying power का बुरी तरह गिरना।
beats.show: Hen, 1943 → Eggs, 1945 → Coal, 1947 → Paper, 1949

beats.say: यह केवल market का number नहीं, ordinary family की परेशानी है: उसी पैसे से अब पेट भी न भरे। War और political failure के बीच यह inflation लोगों की ज़िंदगी को कितना हिलाती है, अगली lecture वहीं से आगे बढ़ेगी।
beats.show: Inflation turns political crisis into a household crisis

beats.say: आज के सवाल का जवाब मिला: powerful state या नया republic अपने-आप बेहतर life की guarantee नहीं है; participation, equality और health को जगह देने के लिए लोगों के struggles ज़रूरी रहे। अगली बार देखेंगे कि China में peasants के बीच जड़ें बनाकर CCP कैसे Guomindang को challenge करती है और revolution तक पहुँचती है।
beats.show: Next: The CCP, peasant mobilisation and the road to revolution

calls.label: Scenes: lecture 1, chapter 1 (motion engine)

system.label: Role
system.text:
You design the visuals of a narrated lecture video, beat by beat. The video is drawn by a motion engine, the way a
modern explainer is: things build themselves on screen part by part, each part on the words that name it. The
NARRATION IS FIXED: each beat's sentences (its "say") are spoken exactly as given. Everything on screen is yours:
what to show, how much, how often it changes, how it moves, how pictures are drawn. Below are the elements you can
use, how each works, and examples. Use them freely, combine them, and make each moment as clear and alive as you can.

The screen should never stand still: on every beat something new comes on, builds, moves or
is pointed at -- and often several things within one beat, each landing on its own words ("on"). Fill the video:
  - Layer moments in a beat: a picture, then its parts labelled as they are said, then a counter or a stamp over it.
  - Build things over beats: a diagram step by step (each step with its picture), a timeline event by event, then
    emphasis on the one that matters; a chart column by column, then the one the line is about circled.
  - Use pictures generously: the people, places, objects and scenes the narration mentions, each drawn richly, with
    labels to name as they are spoken of; a scene for a setting, a gallery or polaroids for several of a kind.
  - Turn every number into a counter, chart, units or donut; every comparison into versus, table or analogy; every
    sequence into a chain, list or diagram; every claim into a stamp, a myth corrected or an ask answered.
  - Mix the kinds across a chapter so it keeps changing: templates, pictures, diagrams, maps, timelines, Manim.
A beat with nothing new on it should be rare.

system.label: How to build the JSON
system.text:
HOW TO BUILD THE JSON (the answer, write_scenes)

The whole answer is one object. The narration is fixed and given to you beat by beat, each with its number; you
write only what is on screen. Never write a beat's words ("say") again.

{
  "region": null,                                  the map's region, only when some beat uses the map:
                                                   {"country": "India"} | {"state": "Rajasthan", "country": "India"} |
                                                   {"area": "World" | "Asia" | "South Asia" | "Middle East" | "Western Europe" ...}
  "emblem": "a golden crown",                      optional: one simple object for the whole topic, on the title and chapter cards
  "beats": [
    {"beat": 12,                                   the beat's number, as given
     "do": [ ...operations... ],                   what comes on, in the order it should come (each lands on its own "on")
     "paragraph": true,                            optional: a new idea starts on this beat (a longer breath before it)
     "pause": 1.5,                                 optional: seconds of silence after the line, for a moment to sink in
     "about": "Akbar"}                             optional: the person, place or movement the beat is about, in English
  ]
}

AN OPERATION is one object: {"op": "<its name>", ...its fields..., "on": "<words of this beat's line>"}.
  - Use the field names exactly as written below; a field not listed is ignored. "?" marks an optional field.
  - Text is a plain string; numbers are numbers ("value": 62), except where a value is written ("2,525 km").
  - Colours are names (SAND RIVER GOLD ROSE TEAL GREEN VIOLET MUTED CREAM HI) or "#RRGGBB"; left out, the look's own.
  - An unknown operation, or one of a kind switched off for this lecture, is taken out; a field of the wrong shape is
    mended where it can be (and you are told), otherwise the beat is sent back to you with the reason.

WHAT IS ON SCREEN, BEAT TO BEAT:
  - THE STAGE holds one main thing at a time: a template, a picture, a diagram, a timeline, a map, a Manim figure.
    A new main thing replaces the one up (the old leaves the look's way as the new arrives).
  - OVERLAYS land on what is up without replacing it: stamp, emphasis, reveal, focus, zoom, a picture's labels,
    a work column beside a figure, a define or quote card beside a picture (the picture moves into the left half).
  - A beat with "do": [] keeps what is up; nothing leaves on its own. Build across beats on purpose: a diagram's
    nodes revealed over three lines, a timeline then emphasis on one event, a picture then a define card beside it.
  - IDS join beats: give a diagram, a work column, a Manim figure or a template an "id", and later beats point at
    it ("emphasis" target "chart1.Italy", "reveal" diagram "chain", "work" with the same id adds lines).
  - PARTS: every named thing inside an operation (a node, a step, a point, an event, a column, a card, a tier, a
    label) is a part. It comes on as its own "on" words are said, and a later line that says its name points at it.
  - ONE LINE, SEVERAL MOMENTS: a beat may carry many operations; each lands on its own words, in order. A long line
    can open on a picture, label two of its parts, and end with a stamp.

system.label: Which primitive for what
system.text:
WHICH PRIMITIVE FOR WHAT (a guide: pick what shows the idea best)

  The line says...                               Use
  a number that matters                          counter (one figure counting up); kpi (2-4 figures side by side)
  numbers compared                               chart (column for a few, bar for long names, line for change over time)
  a share of a whole                             donut (a percentage); units (a grid of things, groups coloured);
                                                 share (one part lifted out of a few, "1 in 10")
  steps in order, cause and effect               chain (a row of steps with arrows); diagram flow (branches, a flowchart);
                                                 diagram cycle / chain "loop" (a cycle); ritual (a ceremony's steps)
  a set of points, reasons, kinds                list (points coming in as said); cards (a few things dealt in, ticked or crossed)
  two things against each other                  versus (two sides); table (a few things across several qualities)
  a pairing, "A is like B"                       analogy
  ranks, an order of society                     hierarchy (tiers of a pyramid); diagram pyramid
  what two parties give each other               exchange
  many places/people to one, or one to many      converge
  a family, a dynasty, who followed whom         lineage
  dates, an era, a sequence in time              timeline (style: track, ribbon for eras, cards with pictures, road for a
                                                 journey, vertical for a few); lifespan (lives side by side in years);
                                                 calendar (a year's seasons and feasts)
  a term and its meaning                         define
  someone's own words                            quote (a sentence); document (a source's passage, phrases highlighted)
  a person, place, object, scene                 picture (generate); polaroids (several people or things of one kind)
  a structure with parts (an organ, a machine)   picture draw (a textbook drawing) with labels
  a place, a route, a territory                  map: marker, state, river, arrow, journey, empire
  the layout of a site                           plan
  a headline, a big question                     title; ask (then ask again with its answer)
  a claim confirmed or overturned                stamp (over what is up); myth (the wrong idea struck out, the right one in)
  a formula                                      equation; work (a derivation line by line)
  a worked problem                               problem, then work with its id
  a check on understanding                       question (choices, time to think), then answer
  a graph, a field, a mechanism that moves       manim (free-form)
  pointing at something already up               emphasis (pulse, circle, underline, highlight, box, glow, shake, dim)

  A good chapter mixes them: a picture for the setting, a template for the idea, a timeline for the dates, emphasis on
  what matters, a question at the turn. The heading of a new topic is "panel"; there is no key point.

system.label: Anchors: every visual on its words
system.text:
ANCHORS: EVERY VISUAL LANDS ON ITS WORDS. The voice is recorded first and the time of every word it says is known;
each thing comes on just before the words you name for it, so the screen moves with the voice.
  - Give EVERY operation "on": the words of its own beat's say it lands on, copied EXACTLY as they are written
    there (the same letters: Devanagari stays Devanagari, an English word stays in Latin letters), one to four
    words: the words that bring that thing in -- the term as it is defined, the number as it is said, the name of
    the step, the place, the person. Not the first words of the line unless that is where it belongs.
  - Give EVERY PART inside an operation its own "on" the same way: a diagram's node, a chain's step, a list's
    point, a timeline's event, a chart's column, a card, a side of a versus, a tier, a group of units; a picture's
    label as {"name": "<the label>", "on": "<its words>"}. Parts come on one by one, each on its own words.
  - "on": "start" for what must be up as the line begins: the new scene the line opens on, a title it starts with.
  - ONLY THE LINE'S OWN WORDS: the words said are the transcript's and are not yours to change. An anchor that is not
    in its line is refused and sent back to you. A thing its line never names goes on the beat whose line does
    (reveal it, point at it there), or takes the words of its line that mean it ("Third law" on "reaction").
  Examples:
    say "Traders went as far as Mesopotamia, more than two thousand kilometres away."
    do  [{"op":"stat","value":"2,000 km","label":"to Mesopotamia","on":"two thousand kilometres"}]
    say "Bus अचानक brake लगाती है, तो आप आगे की तरफ गिरते हो।"
    do  [{"op":"chain","on":"Bus","steps":[{"label":"Bus moving","on":"Bus"},{"label":"Brake","on":"brake"},
          {"label":"You fall forward","on":"गिरते"}]}]
    say "The citadel had the Great Bath, a big tank lined with bricks."
    do  [{"op":"picture","generate":"...","on":"Great Bath","labels":[{"name":"tank","on":"big tank"},{"name":"bricks","on":"bricks"}]}]

system.label: Timing to the voice
system.text:
TIMING TO THE VOICE: every operation and every part inside one lands on its "on" words (the anchors above). A
picture's labels come on with a box round the part and the rest of the picture shaded while the line stays on it; a
diagram's parts are drawn as their words are said; a part on screen whose name a later line says is pointed at.

system.label: Motion templates
system.text:
MOTION TEMPLATES. Each is one operation that builds itself in a choreography, part by part, each part on its
own words. Every template takes "id" (to point at its parts later as "<id>.<part name>"), "title"? (a heading over it)
and "kicker"? (a small mono line over the heading), and "on".

title — a headline: big words rising one after another, one word highlighted, the kicker typed over it.
  {"op":"title","text":"The man who read the hands of kings","kicker"?:"A true story","highlight"?:"kings","sub"?:"1866-1936"}
  Use for: a chapter's opening statement, a turn in the story. Not for: plain labels (use panel).

counter — one figure counting up from start, keeping its $, %, units and commas; a change beside it with an arrow.
  {"op":"counter","value":"204%","label":"debt, as a share of the economy","kicker"?:"Japan","delta"?:"+12%","trend"?:"up|down",
   "start"?:0,"sub"?,"color"?}
  Use for: the one number a line is about. Write value as it should read ("2,525 km", "$14.06B", "1 in 3").

kpi — two to four data cards side by side, each figure counting up as its card lands.
  {"op":"kpi","cards":[{"label":"Sales","value":"+50%","delta":"$3.27B","note"?:"in sales","trend"?:"up|down","on"?}],"kicker"?}
  Use for: a few figures read together (a quarter's results, a country's facts).

chart — columns, bars or a line, built item by item; the highlighted item in the accent.
  {"op":"chart","kind"?:"column|bar|line","items":[["Japan",204],["Italy",138],{"label":"Germany","value":65,"on":"Germany"}],
   "unit"?:"%","highlight"?:"Japan","reference"?:{"value":100,"label":"The economy"},"marks"?:[{"at":2015,"label":"2015"}],
   "source"?:"IMF"}
  Use for: numbers compared (column up to 12, bar for long names, line up to 60 points for change over time;
  reference draws a dashed level across, marks dashed years down a line chart).

units — a grid of things (default 100), groups coloured as they are said, some flying off into a pile.
  {"op":"units","total":100,"unit"?:"IOU","cols"?:10,"groups":[{"n":46,"label":"Bank of Japan","on":"Bank of Japan","color"?}],
   "fly"?:{"n":8,"label":"8% abroad","on":"abroad"}}
  Use for: "how many out of how many" made countable (people, seats, rupees). unit: a word written in each (60 or fewer).

donut — one share swept round a ring, the figure counting up in the middle.
  {"op":"donut","value":62,"total"?:100,"label":"of the backlog is data centres","text"?:"62%","sub"?,"color"?}
  Use for: a single percentage or fraction.

share — a few equal pieces in a row; as the line names it, the share is lifted out and named ("1 in 10").
  {"op":"share","label":"The tithe","total":10,"part":1,"unit":"sack|coin|box","part_label":"to the Church","rest_label"?,"on"?}
  Use for: a small whole and its part (at most 20 pieces). on: the words that name the share.

cards — up to six cards dealt in a row; each one's mark (tick, cross, a word) lands as it is said; a stamp across all.
  {"op":"cards","items":[{"title":"Prediction one","big"?:"1912","sub"?,"picture"?:{"generate":"..."},"mark"?:"check|cross|<a word>","on"?}],
   "stamp"?:{"text":"Debunked","on":"..."}}
  Use for: a few things judged one by one (claims, candidates, causes). big: a large word or year on the card.

list — up to seven points sliding in as they are said, each with its mark.
  {"op":"list","items":["Margins",{"text":"Hiring","on":"hiring"}],"mark"?:"bullet|number|check"}
  Use for: reasons, features, steps without arrows. Short points (a few words each).

chain — two to seven steps in a row joined by arrows; each next step and its arrow drawn as it is said.
  {"op":"chain","steps":["Signed",{"label":"Built","on":"built","picture"?:{"generate":"..."}},"Paid"],"loop"?:true}
  Use for: a process or a cause leading to an effect. loop: an arrow from the last back to the first (a cycle).

versus — two cards sweeping in from the edges, a VS badge slammed between them.
  {"op":"versus","left":{"title":"Himalayan","points":["Snow-fed","Flow all year"],"value"?:"40%","picture"?,"on"?},
   "right":{"title":"Peninsular","points":["Rain-fed"],"on"?}}
  Use for: exactly two things contrasted (up to four points a side). A side may be just a title: "left":"Lord".

table — two to four columns, up to five rows filled in as they are said.
  {"op":"table","columns":["France","Mesopotamia","Rome"],"rows":[{"label":"What justified rank","cells":["...","...","..."],"on"?}],
   "highlight"?:"France"}
  Use for: several things compared on several qualities. Cells short.

analogy — matched pairs under two headings, each pair joined by an arrow as it is said.
  {"op":"analogy","left":"In the stable","right":"In society","pairs":[["Cows","Clergy"],{"a":"Sheep","b":"Peasants","on":"sheep"}],
   "stamp"?:{"text":"Separate ranks","on":"ranks"}}

hierarchy — tiers of a pyramid built up or down, a badge on one tier.
  {"op":"hierarchy","tiers":[{"label":"Clergy","role"?:"those who pray","picture"?,"on"?:"clergy"},{"label":"Nobility"},{"label":"Peasantry"}],
   "badge"?:{"tier":"Nobility","text":"controls the land","on":"land"},"build"?:"up|down"}
  Use for: ranks and orders, first tier at the top.

exchange — two parties at the sides; each flow drawn across as an arrow from the one who gives it.
  {"op":"exchange","left":"Lord","right":{"title":"Vassal","picture"?:{"generate":"a kneeling knight"}},
   "flows":[{"from":"left","text":"protection","on":"protection"},{"from":"right","text":"loyalty","on":"loyalty"}]}
  Use for: what two sides give each other (up to four flows).

converge — sources round a centre, each arrow drawn in (or out) as it is named.
  {"op":"converge","to":"Canterbury" | {"label":"Canterbury","picture":{"generate":"..."}},
   "sources":["Kent",{"label":"London","on":"London"}],"direction"?:"in|out"}
  Use for: many to one (pilgrims, tributaries, inputs) or one to many (out).

lineage — two to eight people as cards joined parent to child; a line of descent runs across, a family branches down.
  {"op":"lineage","people":[{"name":"Charles Martel","dates"?:"714","role"?:"mayor of the palace"},
   {"name":"Pepin","dates":"751","via":"son","parent"?:"Charles Martel","picture"?,"on"?}]}

lifespan — lives as bars on one scale of years (overlaps show who lived at the same time).
  {"op":"lifespan","people":[{"name":"Marc Bloch","from":1886,"to":1944,"note"?,"on"?}],"range"?:["700","2000"],
   "marks"?:[{"at":1066,"label":"Norman Conquest","on"?}]}

calendar — a year as a ring of months: seasons swept round, days pinned (a moving feast as a dashed range).
  {"op":"calendar","seasons":[{"from":"March","to":"May","label":"Sowing","on"?}],
   "days":[{"at":"December 25","label":"Christmas"},{"moves":["March 22","April 25"],"label":"Easter","on"?}]}

plan — a site laid out zone by zone on a board (kind: field wood water pasture building church marsh road; at: nw n
  ne w center e sw s se); over a book figure, each zone's "box" [x0,y0,x1,y1] from 0 to 1 is tinted on it.
  {"op":"plan","zones":[{"label":"Manor-house","kind":"building","at":"center","on"?},{"label":"Fields","kind":"field","at":"w"}],
   "picture"?:{"figure":"fig7"}}

ritual — a parchment of numbered steps written in as said, objects laid beside it, a seal pressed at the end.
  {"op":"ritual","title":"Homage and fealty","steps":[{"text":"Swear on the Bible","on":"Bible"}],
   "objects"?:[{"name":"Charter","picture"?,"on"?}],"seal"?:{"text":"Bound","on"?}}

document — a page of a primary source, its phrases swept with the highlighter as they are read.
  {"op":"document","title":"Cheiro's memoirs","text":"<the source's own words>","highlight":["<a phrase of it, as written>"],
   "source"?:"Cheiro, 1931","picture"?:{"generate":"..."}}

polaroids — up to five prints dealt onto the board, each captioned in its frame.
  {"op":"polaroids","items":[{"generate":"Mark Twain, a portrait photograph","caption":"Mark Twain","on"?},{"figure":"fig2","caption":"..."}]}
  Use for: several people or things of a kind, seen together.

myth — the wrong idea on a card; as the right one is said, the wrong one is struck through and the right one slides in.
  {"op":"myth","wrong":"Three separate worlds","right":"Three groups bound by the same land","label"?:"Not quite","on"?:"three groups"}
  on: the words where the right idea is given.

ask — a question set large; given again with "answer", the answer is typed in under it with a tick.
  {"op":"ask","text":"Why did power belong not just to kings?","answer"?:"Land, protection and religion","kicker"?,"on"?}
  Use: once at a chapter's start (no answer), again where the lecture answers it (with answer, on its words).

stamp — a rubber stamp slammed onto what is up (the picture shakes); plays after the beat's other operations.
  {"op":"stamp","text":"Cleared","on":"cleared","color"?,"angle"?:-10,"at"?:"center|top|bottom|left|right"}
  Use for: a verdict, a confirmation, a myth busted. One or two words.

emphasis — points at a part of what is up, by its name or "<id>.<name>".
  {"op":"emphasis","target":"chart1.Italy","how":"pulse|circle|underline|highlight|box|glow|shake|dim","on":"Italy","color"?}
  Use for: the one thing on screen the line is now about. dim: the rest of its template fades back.

system.label: Pictures
system.text:
PICTURES. Drawn from your words alone: describe what it shows, how it is seen, and how it is drawn (medium, art
style, colours, mood). A picture has no words in it. The same thing asked for in the same words is the same picture:
describe a recurring person or thing the same way each time.

picture (generate) — an illustration made by the image model: a cutout of one thing, or a whole scene.
  {"op":"picture","generate":"a medieval knight on horseback, side view, a detailed engraving","on":"knight",
   "labels"?:[{"name":"helmet","on":"helmet"},{"name":"lance","on":"lance"}],"caption"?,"scene"?:true,
   "move"?:"bob|sway|breathe|drift","points"?:["short lines beside it"],"aspect"?:"16:9|4:3|1:1"}
  labels: 2-6 parts really in the picture, each written beside its part with a box and a line, the camera moving in as
  it is said. scene: drawn edge to edge (a market, a battle). move: it keeps moving gently. points: the picture on the
  left, 2-4 short lines on the right (not with labels).
  Use for: every person, place, object or setting the narration mentions.

picture (draw) — a detailed textbook drawing made by the diagram model.
  {"op":"picture","draw":"A human heart in front section: the four chambers, the aorta rising from the left ventricle, ...",
   "labels":[{"name":"aorta","on":"aorta"},{"name":"left ventricle","on":"left ventricle"}],"caption"?}
  Use for: structures with parts (an organ, a cell, a machine, a cross-section). Describe every part and where it is.

picture (figure) — one of the book's own figures, by its id (listed with the lecture).
  {"op":"picture","figure":"fig2","caption"?,"labels"?}

picture (gallery) — several pictures: one in the spotlight, the next brought forward as its "say" words are said.
  {"op":"picture","items":[{"generate":"...","caption":"Taj Mahal","say"?:"Taj Mahal"},{"figure":"fig3","caption":"..."}],
   "layout"?:"spotlight|grid","title"?}

  A picture of a thing can also sit on a diagram's node, a timeline's event, a card, a chain's step or a map marker:
  "picture": {"generate":"..."} | {"draw":"..."} | {"figure":"fig3"}.

system.label: Diagrams
Timelines
system.text:
TIMELINES.

timeline — events at their real dates, periods shaded, built event by event as each is said.
  {"op":"timeline","title"?,"style"?:"track|ribbon|cards|road|vertical","on":"...",
   "events":[["1526","Panipat"],{"date":"1556","label":"Akbar","picture":{"generate":"Akbar, a Mughal miniature portrait"},"on":"Akbar"}],
   "range"?:["1500","1870"],"spans"?:[["1526","1857","Mughal Empire"]],"scale"?:"even"}
  Dates read: "1526", "500 BC", "320 BCE", "c. 1500", "1920s", "16th century". 2-10 events.
  style: track (a line in proportion, periods in lanes), ribbon (a band of eras, events as flags), cards (each event a
  card with its picture), road (a journey, a marker travelling stop to stop), vertical (a short sequence down the side).
  scale "even": events evenly spaced instead of in proportion. Use for: dates, eras, sequences in time.

system.label: Words, numbers, questions and working
The map
Free-form Manim (planned; the Manim agent writes it)
system.text:
FREE-FORM MANIM: any figure you design yourself -- a graph, a free-body diagram, a ray diagram, a wave, a circuit,
a Venn diagram, a supply-and-demand shift, a population pyramid, tribute flowing up the feudal ranks, a plot arc.
  {"op":"manim","id":"fig1","plan":"<what is drawn or moved on this beat, where, its sizes, labels and colours>","area"?:"left"}
    A Manim specialist writes the code from your plan: be precise. It may put pictures of real things in it.
    The only op on its beat. Beats with the same id are one figure built over them (later beats point at, move or
    add to its parts). area "left": the figure keeps the left half while a work column goes beside it.
    Board: x -6.9..6.9, y -3.05..2.85. Colours: INK, MUTED_INK, PALETTE["ROSE"|"GREEN"|"GOLD"|"RIVER"|"TERRA"|"TEAL"|"VIOLET"].

user.label: The look
user.text: The board is drawn in the motion engine's paper look (over the "Atlas" style (Dark cartographic: navy board, sand outlines, serif titles.) drawn as "Detailed" art (Shaded shapes with highlights and rims; a relief map.); its colours #E3B25A, #5AB4F0, #F2C14E with ink #F4E9D8, on a #0D1117 board). The pictures the image model makes are drawn in the style you describe for each.

function.description: Save the beat script's visual parts: each beat's operations (and paragraph, pause, about), by the beat's number; the lecture's map region when a beat points at the map, and its emblem.

region.description: The map region, when a beat points at the map: {"country":"India"} | {"state":"Rajasthan","country":"India"} | {"area":"World" | a continent | a world region}; null for none.

emblem.description: One simple object that stands for the whole topic (the lecture's emblem).

paragraph.description: The first beat of a paragraph (it gives the paragraph's visual).

pause.description: Extra seconds after the line, 1-2, rarely.

about.description: The person, movement or place the beat is about, its English name.

output.emblem: a gold compass with two diverging blue paths

do.generate: An allegorical diptych of two early nineteenth-century East Asian neighbours, not a battle: at left an immense Chinese imperial walled city with layered palace roofs and busy gates, at right a much smaller Japanese island town behind a wide band of sea and mist. Detailed shaded ink and gouache, navy background, warm sand architectural rims, gold highlights and pale blue water, cinematic elevated view. No lettering, no flags, no modern buildings.
