output.title: China's Revolution: Peasants, Party Power and the Promise of Modernisation
output.about: How the CCP won rural support, transformed China after 1949, and combined market reforms with political control, alongside Taiwan's different path.

chapters.title: A Revolution Needs a Base
chapters.narration: Chapter one, revolution को अपना आधार कहाँ मिला?

beats.say: पिछली बार China की कहानी rising prices और Guomindang की उस कमजोरी पर रुकी थी, जिसमें peasants की problems पीछे छूट गई थीं। अब सवाल है: उन्हीं peasants की मदद से जीतने वाली revolution, क्या उन्हें prosperity के साथ अपनी आवाज़ भी दे पाएगी?
beats.show: Central question: Can revolution deliver prosperity and a political voice?

beats.say: आगे बढ़ने से पहले timeline में कुछ खाली जगहें भर लीजिए। पहले से पढ़े घटनाक्रम को दोहराना नहीं है; बस उन dates को जोड़ना है जो बदलाव की रफ्तार साफ करेंगी।
beats.show: Parallel timelines: Japan and China; previously covered events dimmed

beats.say: Japan में 1603 में Edo shogunate स्थापित करने वाले Tokugawa Ieyasu थे। Timeline 1630 को Western powers के लिए दरवाज़े बंद करने का marker रखती है, Dutch trade के limited exception के साथ; यह 1630s में विकसित restrictions का shorthand है, पूरी दुनिया से कट जाना नहीं।
beats.show: Japan: 1603 — Tokugawa Ieyasu; 1630s — restrictions on Western contact

beats.say: China की Qing dynasty को timeline 1644 से 1911 तक रखती है। उसके भीतर 1839 से 1860 का बड़ा span दोनों Opium Wars को समेटता है; पिछली बार हमने पहली war को करीब से देखा था।
beats.show: China: Qing dynasty, 1644–1911; two Opium Wars, 1839–1860

beats.say: Japan के लिए 1872 compulsory education की formal शुरुआत का marker है, और Meiji Constitution 1889 में enact हुआ। फिर 1925 में universal male suffrage आया; male का मतलब ध्यान रखिए, women को vote अभी नहीं मिला था।
beats.show: Japan: 1872 — compulsory education; 1889 — constitution; 1925 — universal male suffrage

beats.say: Timeline दोनों wars की पूरी dates भी साफ करती है: China के साथ 1894 से 1895, और Russia के साथ 1904 से 1905। Korea की colonial period 1910 से 1945 थी, और First World War का span 1914 से 1918 था।
beats.show: Date anchors: 1894–1895; 1904–1905; Korea, 1910–1945; First World War, 1914–1918

beats.say: China में Sun Yat-sen ने 1912 में Guomindang स्थापित किया। अब civil wars के लिए 1926 से 1949 का लंबा span रखिए; 1949 की जीत किसी एक छोटी लड़ाई का result नहीं थी।
beats.show: China: Guomindang founded, 1912; civil-war era, 1926–1949

beats.say: एक और फर्क: Japan का 1931 वाला invasion Manchuria से जुड़ा है, जबकि 1937 में बड़े पैमाने पर China के साथ war शुरू हुई। Pacific War का span 1941 से 1945 है।
beats.show: 1931 — Manchuria; 1937 — full-scale war in China; 1941–1945 — Pacific War

beats.say: Occupation के लिए timeline 1946 से 1952 लिखती है, लेकिन पूरी US-led Occupation 1945 से 1952 थी। उसके बाद 1956 में Japan United Nations का member बना और 1964 के Tokyo Olympics Asia में होने वाले पहले Olympics थे।
beats.show: Japan: Occupation, 1945–1952; UN membership, 1956; first Olympics in Asia, 1964

beats.say: अब उन dates के पीछे की ज़िंदगी देखिए। 1937 के Japanese invasion के बाद Guomindang पीछे हटा, और लंबी, थका देने वाली war ने पूरे China को कमज़ोर कर दिया।
beats.show: 1937: invasion, retreat and prolonged war

beats.say: 1945 से 1949 के बीच prices हर महीने करीब 30 per cent बढ़ रहे थे। सोचिए, आज जो सामान 100 yuan का है, वही इसी rate पर अगले महीने 130 और उसके बाद 169 yuan का हो जाए।
beats.show: Monthly inflation example: 100 yuan → 130 yuan → 169 yuan

beats.say: यह सिर्फ हर महीने 30 जोड़ना नहीं है; बढ़ी हुई कीमत पर फिर बढ़ोतरी लगती है। Wage उतनी तेज़ न बढ़े, तो किराने की वही छोटी टोकरी भी घर का budget तोड़ देगी।
beats.show: Compounding prices; household purchasing power falling

beats.say: Village में संकट दोहरा था। Soil exhaustion से ज़मीन की उपजाऊ ताकत घट रही थी, forests कट रहे थे और floods नुकसान बढ़ा रहे थे; यह ecological crisis थी।
beats.show: Rural ecological crisis: exhausted soil, deforestation, floods

beats.say: दूसरी तरफ exploitative land-tenure arrangements, कर्ज़, पुरानी technology और खराब communications थे। मतलब किसान की problem केवल खराब मौसम नहीं थी; ज़मीन और कमाई पर उसका control भी कमज़ोर था।
beats.show: Rural socio-economic crisis: land tenure, debt, primitive technology, poor communications

beats.say: अब बताइए, अगर कोई movement इन्हीं problems को अपनी politics के centre में रखे, तो उसका आधार कहाँ बनेगा? जवाब villages में है, और यहीं Mao की strategy अलग हुई।
beats.show: Political opening: the peasantry

chapters.title: Learning from Village Life
chapters.narration: Chapter two, villages से revolution की strategy बनी।

beats.say: CCP 1921 में बनी, Russian Revolution के कुछ ही साल बाद। Russia की सफलता ने दुनिया के बहुत-से लोगों को भरोसा दिया कि exploitation पर टिकी व्यवस्था बदली जा सकती है।
beats.show: 1921: Communist Party of China founded

beats.say: Lenin और Trotsky जैसे leaders से जुड़ा Comintern, यानी Third International, communist movements को international support देने वाला organisation था। उसकी स्थापना March 1919 में हुई थी; किताब में March 1918 आया है, उस date को correct कर लीजिए।
beats.show: Comintern / Third International: founded March 1919

beats.say: उसका घोषित goal exploitation खत्म करने वाली world government की दिशा में काम करना था। Soviet Union और Comintern ने अलग-अलग देशों की communist parties को support दिया।
beats.show: International communist support; stated goal: ending exploitation

beats.say: लेकिन traditional Marxist understanding में revolution का मुख्य आधार city की working class थी। फैक्ट्रियों में साथ काम करने वाले workers संगठित होकर सत्ता बदलेंगे, यही उम्मीद थी।
beats.show: Traditional expectation: urban working-class revolution

beats.say: Comintern की शुरुआती appeal national boundaries के पार बहुत बड़ी थी। मगर बाद में वह Soviet interests का tool बनता गया, और 1943 में उसे dissolve कर दिया गया।
beats.show: Comintern: international appeal → Soviet priorities → dissolution, 1943

beats.say: Mao Zedong, जो 1893 से 1976 तक रहे, ने China की conditions देखकर अलग रास्ता चुना। उन्होंने peasants को अपने revolutionary programme का आधार बनाया, और इसी strategy ने CCP को बड़ी political force बनने में मदद की।
beats.show: Mao Zedong, 1893–1976: a peasant-based revolutionary strategy

beats.say: Map पर southeastern China में Jiangxi पहचानिए। Mountains में CCP ने 1928 से 1934 तक base बनाया, जहाँ शुरुआत में Guomindang के attacks से काफी सुरक्षा मिलती थी।
beats.show: Map: Jiangxi mountain base, 1928–1934

beats.say: वहाँ strong peasants' council, यानी soviet, organise हुआ। यहाँ soviet का मतलब council है; हर बार यह शब्द Soviet Union देश का नाम नहीं है।
beats.show: Key term: soviet — a council

beats.say: Land confiscate करके redistribute की गई। सोचिए, अगर आपकी खेती और आपकी livelihood पर movement सीधा असर डाल रही है, तो politics दूर की speech नहीं रहती।
beats.show: Land confiscation and redistribution build a rural base

beats.say: Mao ने independent government और अपनी army की ज़रूरत पर भी ज़ोर दिया। केवल protest करना नहीं, अपने फैसले लागू करने और base बचाने की capacity भी चाहिए थी।
beats.show: Organisation: council + independent government + army

beats.say: उन्होंने rural women's associations को support किया। नई marriage law ने arranged marriages पर रोक लगाई, marriage contracts की खरीद-बिक्री बंद की और divorce को आसान बनाया।
beats.show: Women's associations; marriage reform; simpler divorce

beats.say: अब एक गलत impression से बचिए: peasants को support करना सिर्फ उन्हें अच्छी speeches देना नहीं था। Mao ने उनकी रोज़ की economy को समझने के लिए detailed investigations भी कीं।
beats.show: From slogans to investigation

beats.say: 1930 में Xunwu के survey में उन्होंने salt और soya beans जैसी everyday commodities देखीं। Local organisations कितनी strong हैं, petty traders और craftsmen कैसे रहते हैं, यह भी पूछा।
beats.show: Xunwu survey, 1930: commodities, organisations, livelihoods

beats.say: Ironsmiths, prostitutes और religious organisations तक को इस study में शामिल किया गया। अलग-अलग groups को देखकर वे समझना चाहते थे कि exploitation किस level पर और किस रूप में हो रहा है।
beats.show: Survey scope: crafts, sex work, religion and local power

beats.say: उन्होंने उन peasants की संख्या और मिले हुए पैसे भी दर्ज किए, जिन्हें अपने children बेचने पड़े थे। Survey में boys के लिए 100 से 200 yuan मिले; यह गरीबी की बहुत दर्दनाक हद थी।
beats.show: Survey evidence: boys sold for 100–200 yuan

beats.say: उस particular investigation में girls की sale के cases नहीं मिले। Mao का explanation था कि यहाँ demand hard labour के लिए थी, sexual exploitation के लिए नहीं; इसे पूरे China में girls कभी बेची नहीं गईं, ऐसा claim मत बना दीजिए।
beats.show: Local finding, not a universal claim

beats.say: इन studies के आधार पर उन्होंने social problems के solutions सुझाए। किताब की बात का असली point यह है: programme को लोगों की actual conditions से जोड़ना था।
beats.show: Investigation → diagnosis → social programme

chapters.title: The Long Road to Power
chapters.narration: Chapter three, पीछे हटकर एक नया आधार बना।

beats.say: लेकिन Jiangxi का base हमेशा सुरक्षित नहीं रहा। Guomindang की blockade ने Communists को नया base खोजने के लिए मजबूर कर दिया।
beats.show: Jiangxi base under blockade

beats.say: इसी से 1934 से 1935 का Long March शुरू हुआ, करीब 6,000 miles का बेहद कठिन सफर। यह जीत का आरामदायक जुलूस नहीं था, survival के लिए किया गया retreat था।
beats.show: Long March, 1934–1935: about 6,000 miles

beats.say: Map में solid arrowed line को Juichin से follow कीजिए, जो Kiangsi यानी Jiangxi में है। Route पहले west जाता है, Yunnan और Szechwan से घूमता है, फिर north की तरफ मुड़ता है।
beats.show: Trace main route: Juichin → Yunnan → Szechwan → north

beats.say: Yellow shading Communist areas दिखाती है और dotted arrows दूसरे routes। Main route Yenan, यानी Yanan, के आसपास के northern base की तरफ पहुँचता है; यह सीधी north जाने वाली छोटी line नहीं है।
beats.show: Map key: Communist areas, main route, other routes; endpoint near Yanan

beats.say: नीचे Yangtze और ऊपर Huang He, यानी Yellow River, से दिशा पकड़ सकते हैं। मंज़िल northern Shaanxi थी; किताब का Shanxi spelling अलग province से confusion करा सकता है।
beats.show: Northern Shaanxi; Yanan relative to the Yellow River

beats.say: इस image में खड़ी, uneven ढलान और आगे झुके हुए लोगों को देखिए। उससे difficult terrain और physical effort समझ आता है, लेकिन अकेली image से हर व्यक्ति का काम या exact moment तय नहीं कर सकते।
beats.show: Steep slope, figures and physical effort

beats.say: साथ का caption इसे 1941 में soldiers के wasteland reclaim करने से जोड़ता है। Date ध्यान रखिए: 1941 Long March के बाद है, इसलिए इसे 1934 से 1935 के march का उसी समय लिया गया दृश्य नहीं मानेंगे।
beats.show: Caption date: 1941; Long March dates: 1934–1935

beats.say: Yanan के नए base में programme और विकसित हुआ: warlordism खत्म करना, land reforms करना और foreign imperialism से लड़ना। इन goals ने CCP का social base मजबूत किया।
beats.show: Yanan programme: end warlordism, reform land, resist imperialism

beats.say: Japanese war के कठिन वर्षों में Communists और Guomindang ने साथ भी काम किया। दो rivals कभी common enemy के सामने cooperation कर सकते हैं; इसका मतलब उनकी अपनी लड़ाई खत्म हो गई, यह नहीं।
beats.show: Wartime cooperation; continuing rivalry

beats.say: War के बाद struggle फिर सत्ता के फैसले तक पहुँची, और Guomindang हार गया। 1949 में CCP mainland China की नई government बनाने की स्थिति में आ गई।
beats.show: 1949: Communist victory on the mainland

chapters.title: Revolution Becomes Government
chapters.narration: Chapter four, अब revolution को देश चलाना था।

beats.say: 1949 में People's Republic of China स्थापित हुई। मगर लड़ाई जीतने और खेती, industry तथा government चलाने की problems एक जैसी नहीं हैं।
beats.show: 1949: People's Republic of China

beats.say: शुरुआत New Democracy के idea पर हुई, यानी सभी social classes का alliance। इसे Soviet Union के उस claim से अलग रखा गया कि वहाँ dictatorship of the proletariat स्थापित हो चुकी है।
beats.show: New Democracy: an alliance of social classes

beats.say: Proletariat का मतलब working class है। Marx ने dictatorship of the proletariat से propertied class की repressive government की जगह revolutionary working-class government आने की बात की थी, न कि आज के everyday अर्थ वाली personal dictatorship की definition दी थी।
beats.show: Key term: dictatorship of the proletariat — Marx's revolutionary class-government concept

beats.say: फिर भी किसी government का यह term इस्तेमाल करना साबित नहीं करता कि व्यवहार में सबको freedom मिल गई। Concept और actual political system को अलग परखना पड़ता है।
beats.show: Distinguish a political concept from political practice

beats.say: Critical economic sectors government control में आए। Private enterprise और private landownership को धीरे-धीरे खत्म करने की दिशा में कदम हुए; शुरुआती programme 1953 तक चला, जब socialist transformation का programme घोषित हुआ।
beats.show: 1949–1953: state control expands; 1953: socialist transformation

beats.say: अब imagine कीजिए, कोई कहे कि industry को बहुत तेज़ बढ़ाने के लिए हर मोहल्ला अपना steel बनाने लगे। क्या केवल जोश और furnace लगा देने से usable steel तैयार हो जाएगा?
beats.show: Question: Can enthusiasm replace industrial organisation?

beats.say: 1958 का Great Leap Forward देश को बहुत तेज़ industrialise करने की mass campaign थी। लोगों को backyard में steel furnaces बनाने के लिए encourage किया गया।
beats.show: Great Leap Forward, 1958: backyard steel furnaces

beats.say: Villages में people's communes बने, जहाँ land collectively owned और cultivated होती थी। यानी खेत केवल कई पड़ोसी farms की line नहीं रहा; ownership और cultivation का collective arrangement था।
beats.show: People's commune: collective ownership and cultivation

beats.say: 1958 तक 26,000 communes बन चुके थे, जिनमें farm population का 98 per cent cover हुआ। इसलिए यह कोई छोटा experiment नहीं था; लगभग पूरा rural farming world इससे जुड़ गया।
beats.show: 1958: 26,000 communes; 98% of farm population

beats.say: Mao masses को Party के goals के लिए mobilise कर सकते थे। वे ऐसा socialist man बनाना चाहते थे जिसके five loves हों: fatherland, people, labour, science और public property।
beats.show: Socialist person: love of fatherland, people, labour, science and public property

beats.say: Farmers, women, students और दूसरे groups के लिए mass organisations बने। All-China Democratic Women's Federation में सात करोड़ साठ लाख members थे, और All-China Students Federation में बत्तीस लाख नब्बे हज़ार।
beats.show: Mass organisations: Women's Federation — 76 million; Students Federation — 3.29 million

beats.say: लेकिन बड़ी membership और mass enthusiasm से efficient production की guarantee मिलती है? Backyard furnaces से बना steel industrial use के लायक नहीं निकला।
beats.show: Production problem: backyard steel unusable industrially

beats.say: Party में सब Mao के methods से agree नहीं करते थे। 1953 से 1954 में ही कुछ leaders industrial organisation और economic growth पर ज़्यादा ध्यान माँग रहे थे।
beats.show: Early disagreement: organisation and growth versus ideological mobilisation

beats.say: Liu Shaochi, जो 1896 से 1969 तक रहे, और Deng Xiaoping, जो 1904 से 1997 तक रहे, ने inefficient commune system में changes चाहीं। अब tension समझिए: committed होना ज़रूरी है, लेकिन क्या commitment technical expertise की जगह ले सकती है?
beats.show: Liu Shaochi and Deng Xiaoping: modify inefficient communes

beats.say: इस दौर में national strength का military dimension भी बना रहा। Timeline 1962 में border dispute पर China के India पर attack को दर्ज करती है; modernisation के साथ neighbouring states से conflict भी चल रहा था।
beats.show: 1962: Sino-Indian border war; China attacks India

chapters.title: Ideology Against Expertise
chapters.narration: Chapter five, Party के भीतर का conflict society तक फैल गया।

beats.say: सोचिए, hospital में आपको operation कराना है। आप doctor से सिर्फ सही political slogans सुनना चाहेंगे, या उसकी professional knowledge भी जाँचेंगे?
beats.show: Expertise matters: a hospital example

beats.say: China के conflict में यही फर्क बहुत बड़ा था। Maoists socialist person बनाने पर ज़ोर देते थे, जबकि critics कहते थे कि ideology को expertise से ऊपर रखना गलत है।
beats.show: Conflict: ideological commitment versus professional expertise

beats.say: Critics का मुकाबला करने के लिए Mao ने Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution शुरू की। किताब का paragraph 1965 कहता है, लेकिन इसकी formal शुरुआत 1966 मानी जाती है; timeline भी 1966 देती है।
beats.show: Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution: formally launched in 1966

beats.say: Red Guards मुख्य रूप से students के groups थे; campaign में army की भी भूमिका रही। Old culture, old customs और old habits के खिलाफ mobilisation की गई।
beats.show: Red Guards, students and army; campaign against old culture, customs and habits

beats.say: Students और professionals को countryside भेजा गया, ताकि वे masses से सीखें। Problem rural people से सीखना नहीं थी; problem थी professional knowledge को political loyalty से कम important बना देना।
beats.show: Sent to the countryside; political loyalty privileged over expertise

beats.say: Rational debate की जगह denunciations और slogans लेने लगे। Denunciation मतलब किसी को publicly दोषी ठहराना; ऐसे माहौल में evidence के सहारे disagreement करना कठिन हो जाता है।
beats.show: Reasoned debate displaced by public denunciations and slogans

beats.say: Cultural Revolution ने turmoil पैदा किया, Party को कमजोर किया और economy तथा education system को बुरी तरह disrupt किया। इसलिए इसे केवल पुराने customs बदलने की cultural activity समझना बहुत बड़ी भूल होगी।
beats.show: Consequences: turmoil; weakened Party; disrupted economy and education

beats.say: Late 1960s से दिशा बदलने लगी। 1975 में Party ने फिर social discipline और industrial economy पर ज़ोर दिया, ताकि century के अंत तक China बड़ी power बने।
beats.show: Late 1960s: shift begins; 1975: discipline and industrial development

beats.say: 1976 में Mao Zedong और Zhou Enlai, दोनों की death हुई। इसके बाद political manoeuvring का दौर आया, और development का रास्ता फिर नए सिरे से तय होने लगा।
beats.show: 1976: deaths of Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai

chapters.title: Markets Without Political Competition
chapters.narration: Chapter six, economy खुली, लेकिन politics की सीमा बनी रही।

beats.say: Deng Xiaoping के दौर में socialist market economy शुरू हुई, लेकिन Party का control मजबूत रखा गया। यहाँ twist है: economic liberalisation और political liberalisation साथ-साथ होना ज़रूरी नहीं।
beats.show: Deng's approach: market reforms + continued Party control

beats.say: Economic liberalisation में buying, selling और enterprise के लिए ज़्यादा जगह खुल सकती है। Political liberalisation का सवाल अलग है: क्या citizens ruling Party को openly challenge कर सकते हैं?
beats.show: Economic freedom is not the same as political freedom

beats.say: 1978 में Party ने Four Modernisations को goal बनाया: science, industry, agriculture और defence का development। Debate की permission थी, लेकिन उस सीमा तक जहाँ Party की authority पर सवाल न उठे।
beats.show: Four Modernisations, 1978: science, industry, agriculture, defence

beats.say: नए माहौल में ideas की तेज़ हलचल हुई, जैसी करीब साठ साल पहले May Fourth के समय हुई थी। फिर 5 December 1978 को एक wall-poster ने पूछा: एक fifth modernisation क्यों नहीं?
beats.show: 5 December 1978: The Fifth Modernisation wall-poster

beats.say: उस fifth modernisation का नाम था democracy। Poster का argument था कि democracy के बिना बाकी modernisations अपने goals तक नहीं पहुँचेंगी।
beats.show: The Fifth Modernisation: democracy

beats.say: उसने CCP की criticism की कि poverty और sexual exploitation खत्म नहीं हुए। Party के भीतर abuse के examples भी दिए गए; इसलिए challenge सिर्फ economic technique का नहीं, power की accountability का था।
beats.show: Criticism: persistent poverty, sexual exploitation and abuse within the Party

beats.say: इस photograph में दो लोग straps से television set ले जा रहे हैं। 1978 reforms के बाद consumer goods freely खरीदने की बढ़ी हुई गुंजाइश को यह everyday scene दिखाता है।
beats.show: Consumer purchases after reform: carrying a television

beats.say: लेकिन नया television और नया voting right एक ही चीज़ नहीं हैं। Democracy की demands suppress की गईं, भले consumer choice बढ़ रही थी।
beats.show: Consumer choice expands; political demands suppressed

beats.say: 1989 में May Fourth की seventieth anniversary पर intellectuals ने greater openness माँगी। वे ossified dogmas, यानी ऐसी जड़ हो चुकी मान्यताओं से छुटकारा चाहते थे जिन्हें सवालों से बचाकर रखा जाए।
beats.show: 1989: openness and criticism of ossified dogmas; Su Shaozhi

beats.say: Beijing के Tiananmen Square में student demonstrators को brutally repress किया गया। दुनिया भर में इसकी कड़ी condemnation हुई।
beats.show: Tiananmen Square, Beijing, 1989: repression and international condemnation

beats.say: तो post-reform development पर debate खत्म नहीं हुई। Party-backed dominant view में strong political control, economic liberalisation और world market से integration साथ चलते हैं।
beats.show: Dominant model: political control + liberalisation + global integration

beats.say: Critics पूछते हैं कि market पर इतना heavy emphasis किसके लिए काम कर रहा है। Social groups, regions और men तथा women के बीच बढ़ती inequalities social tensions पैदा कर रही हैं।
beats.show: Critiques: inequalities across classes, regions and gender

beats.say: एक और surprising बदलाव हुआ: Confucianism जैसे पहले criticised traditional ideas फिर revive होने लगे। कुछ लोगों ने कहा कि China अपनी traditions के सहारे modern society बना सकता है, केवल West की copy बनकर नहीं।
beats.show: Revival of Confucianism; a debate over a distinct Chinese modernity

beats.say: Timeline का 1997 वाला marker भी जोड़ लें: Britain ने Hong Kong China को वापस किया। Sovereignty का वही पुराना सवाल नए रूप में इस दौर तक बना रहा।
beats.show: 1997: Britain returns Hong Kong to China

beats.say: अब book का essay question सीधे पूछता है: क्या Mao और CCP China को liberate करने और उसकी current success की foundation रखने में successful हुए? सोचिए, केवल हाँ या नहीं लिखने से कौन-सी आधी कहानी छूट जाएगी?
beats.show: Essay question: Did Mao and the CCP liberate China and lay the basis for its current success?

beats.say: Success के पक्ष में rural mobilisation, land redistribution, foreign imperialism के विरोध और 1949 में mainland पर नई central government बनाने का evidence है। Education का फैलाव, पुरानी inequalities पर चोट और organised development की foundation भी इस assessment का हिस्सा हैं।
beats.show: Achievements: rural mobilisation, land reform, sovereignty, education and state-building

beats.say: लेकिन liberation को political freedom भी मानें, तो answer बहुत सीमित हो जाता है। Centralised Party control, Great Leap की production failures और Cultural Revolution में education तथा economy की disruption को अनदेखा नहीं कर सकते।
beats.show: Limits: repression, failed policies and disruption

beats.say: आज की economic strength को केवल Mao की policies की सीधी continuation भी नहीं कह सकते। 1978 के बाद market reforms ने पहले के methods से बड़ा departure लिया, इसलिए foundation और बाद में हुए policy changes, दोनों explain करने होंगे।
beats.show: Balanced judgment: earlier foundations + major post-1978 policy changes

chapters.title: Taiwan's Different Path
chapters.narration: Chapter seven, Taiwan में development और democracy का रिश्ता अलग निकला।

beats.say: 1949 की mainland victory का दूसरा सिरा Taiwan में है। Map पर China के southeast coast से समुद्र पार इस island को पहचानिए।
beats.show: Map: Taiwan and the Taiwan Strait

beats.say: Chiang Kai-shek CCP से हारकर वहाँ गए, साथ में 30 करोड़ US dollar से ज़्यादा के gold reserves और priceless art treasures की crates थीं। इतनी बड़ी financial और cultural संपत्ति भी उस retreat का हिस्सा थी।
beats.show: 1949: Chiang retreats with over US$300 million in gold reserves and art treasures

beats.say: किताब कहती है कि उन्होंने वहाँ Republic of China स्थापित की। ज़्यादा ठीक बात यह है कि पहले से मौजूद Republic of China की government Taiwan चली गई; republic की शुरुआत 1949 में नहीं हुई थी।
beats.show: 1949: Republic of China government relocates to Taiwan

beats.say: Taiwan को China ने 1894 से 1895 की war के बाद Japan को cede किया था और वह Japanese colony बना। फिर 1943 की Cairo Declaration और Potsdam Proclamation ने उसके China को लौटाए जाने की Allied policy रखी।
beats.show: Taiwan: Japanese colony from 1895; Cairo, 1943; Potsdam, 1945

beats.say: यहाँ date correction ज़रूरी है: Potsdam Proclamation 1945 की थी, 1949 की नहीं। 1945 में Republic of China ने Taiwan का administration संभाला; sovereignty और बाद के legal status को लेकर disputes को एक line में खत्म नहीं मान सकते।
beats.show: Correction: Potsdam Proclamation, 1945; distinguish administration from disputed legal status

beats.say: Taiwan की politics में repression पहले से शुरू हो चुकी थी। February 1947 की massive demonstrations के बाद Guomindang ने brutal killings कीं, जिनमें local society के बहुत-से leading figures मारे गए।
beats.show: February 1947: demonstrations followed by violent repression

beats.say: Chiang के under free speech और political opposition पर रोक लगी। Local Taiwanese को positions of power से बाहर रखा गया; इसलिए mainland की communist government से अलग होना अपने-आप democracy होना नहीं था।
beats.show: Authoritarian rule: censorship, suppressed opposition, exclusion of local Taiwanese

beats.say: लेकिन government ने land reforms भी किए, जिनसे agricultural productivity बढ़ी और economy modernise हुई। वही government economic change ला सकती है और political rights दबा सकती है, यह फर्क फिर सामने है।
beats.show: Land reform → agricultural productivity → economic modernisation

beats.say: किताब 1973 तक Taiwan के GNP को Asia में Japan के बाद दूसरे स्थान पर रखती है। इस comparison में per person और total output का फर्क साफ नहीं है, इसलिए इसे total Asian GNP की verified ranking की तरह याद मत कीजिए।
beats.show: 1973 GNP comparison: distinguish total output from per-capita output

beats.say: यहाँ historical point है Taiwan की तेज़ economic growth और trade पर बड़ी dependence। किताब इस growth के साथ rich और poor के बीच gap घटने को भी खास महत्व देती है।
beats.show: Trade-dependent growth; a narrowing rich–poor gap in the account

beats.say: अब बताइए, economic change के साथ क्या authoritarian politics हमेशा वैसी ही रही? नहीं, Chiang की 1975 में death के बाद democratic transition धीरे-धीरे आगे बढ़ा।
beats.show: After 1975: gradual democratic transition

beats.say: 1987 में martial law उठा और opposition parties को legal permission मिली। Free elections ने local Taiwanese को सत्ता तक पहुँचाने का रास्ता खोला।
beats.show: 1987: martial law lifted; opposition permitted; elections broaden local participation

beats.say: इसका मतलब यह नहीं कि repression भूलकर growth की तारीफ कर दें। Democracy का change important इसलिए है कि जिन लोगों को power से बाहर रखा गया था, उन्हें political voice मिली।
beats.show: Democratisation: political inclusion, not merely higher income

beats.say: Taiwan की international position अलग तरह की मुश्किल है। बहुत-से countries embassies के बजाय trade missions रखते हैं, क्योंकि उनकी One China policies Taiwan को sovereign state की तरह recognise करने को सीमित करती हैं।
beats.show: Diplomacy: trade missions, limited formal recognition and One China policies

beats.say: किताब full diplomatic relations को असंभव कहती है, लेकिन यह absolute statement नहीं है; कुछ countries Taiwan की government से formal diplomatic relations रखते हैं। Taiwan अपना administration चलाता है और People's Republic of China उस पर sovereignty claim करती है।
beats.show: Distinguish self-government, sovereignty claims and diplomatic recognition

beats.say: Mainland के साथ reunification विवाद वाला सवाल बना रहा। Cross-Strait relations का मतलब इसी strait के दोनों तरफ Taiwan और mainland China के बीच relations है।
beats.show: Key term: Cross-Strait relations — Taiwan and mainland China

calls.label: Scenes: lecture 1, chapter 3 (motion engine)

system.label: Role
system.text:
You design the visuals of a narrated lecture video, beat by beat. The video is drawn by a motion engine, the way a
modern explainer is: things build themselves on screen part by part, each part on the words that name it. The
NARRATION IS FIXED: each beat's sentences (its "say") are spoken exactly as given. Everything on screen is yours:
what to show, how much, how often it changes, how it moves, how pictures are drawn. Below are the elements you can
use, how each works, and examples. Use them freely, combine them, and make each moment as clear and alive as you can.

The screen should never stand still: on every beat something new comes on, builds, moves or
is pointed at -- and often several things within one beat, each landing on its own words ("on"). Fill the video:
  - Layer moments in a beat: a picture, then its parts labelled as they are said, then a counter or a stamp over it.
  - Build things over beats: a diagram step by step (each step with its picture), a timeline event by event, then
    emphasis on the one that matters; a chart column by column, then the one the line is about circled.
  - Use pictures generously: the people, places, objects and scenes the narration mentions, each drawn richly, with
    labels to name as they are spoken of; a scene for a setting, a gallery or polaroids for several of a kind.
  - Turn every number into a counter, chart, units or donut; every comparison into versus, table or analogy; every
    sequence into a chain, list or diagram; every claim into a stamp, a myth corrected or an ask answered.
  - Mix the kinds across a chapter so it keeps changing: templates, pictures, diagrams, maps, timelines, Manim.
A beat with nothing new on it should be rare.

system.label: How to build the JSON
system.text:
HOW TO BUILD THE JSON (the answer, write_scenes)

The whole answer is one object. The narration is fixed and given to you beat by beat, each with its number; you
write only what is on screen. Never write a beat's words ("say") again.

{
  "region": null,                                  the map's region, only when some beat uses the map:
                                                   {"country": "India"} | {"state": "Rajasthan", "country": "India"} |
                                                   {"area": "World" | "Asia" | "South Asia" | "Middle East" | "Western Europe" ...}
  "emblem": "a golden crown",                      optional: one simple object for the whole topic, on the title and chapter cards
  "beats": [
    {"beat": 12,                                   the beat's number, as given
     "do": [ ...operations... ],                   what comes on, in the order it should come (each lands on its own "on")
     "paragraph": true,                            optional: a new idea starts on this beat (a longer breath before it)
     "pause": 1.5,                                 optional: seconds of silence after the line, for a moment to sink in
     "about": "Akbar"}                             optional: the person, place or movement the beat is about, in English
  ]
}

AN OPERATION is one object: {"op": "<its name>", ...its fields..., "on": "<words of this beat's line>"}.
  - Use the field names exactly as written below; a field not listed is ignored. "?" marks an optional field.
  - Text is a plain string; numbers are numbers ("value": 62), except where a value is written ("2,525 km").
  - Colours are names (SAND RIVER GOLD ROSE TEAL GREEN VIOLET MUTED CREAM HI) or "#RRGGBB"; left out, the look's own.
  - An unknown operation, or one of a kind switched off for this lecture, is taken out; a field of the wrong shape is
    mended where it can be (and you are told), otherwise the beat is sent back to you with the reason.

WHAT IS ON SCREEN, BEAT TO BEAT:
  - THE STAGE holds one main thing at a time: a template, a picture, a diagram, a timeline, a map, a Manim figure.
    A new main thing replaces the one up (the old leaves the look's way as the new arrives).
  - OVERLAYS land on what is up without replacing it: stamp, emphasis, reveal, focus, zoom, a picture's labels,
    a work column beside a figure, a define or quote card beside a picture (the picture moves into the left half).
  - A beat with "do": [] keeps what is up; nothing leaves on its own. Build across beats on purpose: a diagram's
    nodes revealed over three lines, a timeline then emphasis on one event, a picture then a define card beside it.
  - IDS join beats: give a diagram, a work column, a Manim figure or a template an "id", and later beats point at
    it ("emphasis" target "chart1.Italy", "reveal" diagram "chain", "work" with the same id adds lines).
  - PARTS: every named thing inside an operation (a node, a step, a point, an event, a column, a card, a tier, a
    label) is a part. It comes on as its own "on" words are said, and a later line that says its name points at it.
  - ONE LINE, SEVERAL MOMENTS: a beat may carry many operations; each lands on its own words, in order. A long line
    can open on a picture, label two of its parts, and end with a stamp.

system.label: Which primitive for what
system.text:
WHICH PRIMITIVE FOR WHAT (a guide: pick what shows the idea best)

  The line says...                               Use
  a number that matters                          counter (one figure counting up); kpi (2-4 figures side by side)
  numbers compared                               chart (column for a few, bar for long names, line for change over time)
  a share of a whole                             donut (a percentage); units (a grid of things, groups coloured);
                                                 share (one part lifted out of a few, "1 in 10")
  steps in order, cause and effect               chain (a row of steps with arrows); diagram flow (branches, a flowchart);
                                                 diagram cycle / chain "loop" (a cycle); ritual (a ceremony's steps)
  a set of points, reasons, kinds                list (points coming in as said); cards (a few things dealt in, ticked or crossed)
  two things against each other                  versus (two sides); table (a few things across several qualities)
  a pairing, "A is like B"                       analogy
  ranks, an order of society                     hierarchy (tiers of a pyramid); diagram pyramid
  what two parties give each other               exchange
  many places/people to one, or one to many      converge
  a family, a dynasty, who followed whom         lineage
  dates, an era, a sequence in time              timeline (style: track, ribbon for eras, cards with pictures, road for a
                                                 journey, vertical for a few); lifespan (lives side by side in years);
                                                 calendar (a year's seasons and feasts)
  a term and its meaning                         define
  someone's own words                            quote (a sentence); document (a source's passage, phrases highlighted)
  a person, place, object, scene                 picture (generate); polaroids (several people or things of one kind)
  a structure with parts (an organ, a machine)   picture draw (a textbook drawing) with labels
  a place, a route, a territory                  map: marker, state, river, arrow, journey, empire
  the layout of a site                           plan
  a headline, a big question                     title; ask (then ask again with its answer)
  a claim confirmed or overturned                stamp (over what is up); myth (the wrong idea struck out, the right one in)
  a formula                                      equation; work (a derivation line by line)
  a worked problem                               problem, then work with its id
  a check on understanding                       question (choices, time to think), then answer
  a graph, a field, a mechanism that moves       manim (free-form)
  pointing at something already up               emphasis (pulse, circle, underline, highlight, box, glow, shake, dim)

  A good chapter mixes them: a picture for the setting, a template for the idea, a timeline for the dates, emphasis on
  what matters, a question at the turn. The heading of a new topic is "panel"; there is no key point.

system.label: Anchors: every visual on its words
system.text:
ANCHORS: EVERY VISUAL LANDS ON ITS WORDS. The voice is recorded first and the time of every word it says is known;
each thing comes on just before the words you name for it, so the screen moves with the voice.
  - Give EVERY operation "on": the words of its own beat's say it lands on, copied EXACTLY as they are written
    there (the same letters: Devanagari stays Devanagari, an English word stays in Latin letters), one to four
    words: the words that bring that thing in -- the term as it is defined, the number as it is said, the name of
    the step, the place, the person. Not the first words of the line unless that is where it belongs.
  - Give EVERY PART inside an operation its own "on" the same way: a diagram's node, a chain's step, a list's
    point, a timeline's event, a chart's column, a card, a side of a versus, a tier, a group of units; a picture's
    label as {"name": "<the label>", "on": "<its words>"}. Parts come on one by one, each on its own words.
  - "on": "start" for what must be up as the line begins: the new scene the line opens on, a title it starts with.
  - ONLY THE LINE'S OWN WORDS: the words said are the transcript's and are not yours to change. An anchor that is not
    in its line is refused and sent back to you. A thing its line never names goes on the beat whose line does
    (reveal it, point at it there), or takes the words of its line that mean it ("Third law" on "reaction").
  Examples:
    say "Traders went as far as Mesopotamia, more than two thousand kilometres away."
    do  [{"op":"stat","value":"2,000 km","label":"to Mesopotamia","on":"two thousand kilometres"}]
    say "Bus अचानक brake लगाती है, तो आप आगे की तरफ गिरते हो।"
    do  [{"op":"chain","on":"Bus","steps":[{"label":"Bus moving","on":"Bus"},{"label":"Brake","on":"brake"},
          {"label":"You fall forward","on":"गिरते"}]}]
    say "The citadel had the Great Bath, a big tank lined with bricks."
    do  [{"op":"picture","generate":"...","on":"Great Bath","labels":[{"name":"tank","on":"big tank"},{"name":"bricks","on":"bricks"}]}]

system.label: Timing to the voice
system.text:
TIMING TO THE VOICE: every operation and every part inside one lands on its "on" words (the anchors above). A
picture's labels come on with a box round the part and the rest of the picture shaded while the line stays on it; a
diagram's parts are drawn as their words are said; a part on screen whose name a later line says is pointed at.

system.label: Motion templates
system.text:
MOTION TEMPLATES. Each is one operation that builds itself in a choreography, part by part, each part on its
own words. Every template takes "id" (to point at its parts later as "<id>.<part name>"), "title"? (a heading over it)
and "kicker"? (a small mono line over the heading), and "on".

title — a headline: big words rising one after another, one word highlighted, the kicker typed over it.
  {"op":"title","text":"The man who read the hands of kings","kicker"?:"A true story","highlight"?:"kings","sub"?:"1866-1936"}
  Use for: a chapter's opening statement, a turn in the story. Not for: plain labels (use panel).

counter — one figure counting up from start, keeping its $, %, units and commas; a change beside it with an arrow.
  {"op":"counter","value":"204%","label":"debt, as a share of the economy","kicker"?:"Japan","delta"?:"+12%","trend"?:"up|down",
   "start"?:0,"sub"?,"color"?}
  Use for: the one number a line is about. Write value as it should read ("2,525 km", "$14.06B", "1 in 3").

kpi — two to four data cards side by side, each figure counting up as its card lands.
  {"op":"kpi","cards":[{"label":"Sales","value":"+50%","delta":"$3.27B","note"?:"in sales","trend"?:"up|down","on"?}],"kicker"?}
  Use for: a few figures read together (a quarter's results, a country's facts).

chart — columns, bars or a line, built item by item; the highlighted item in the accent.
  {"op":"chart","kind"?:"column|bar|line","items":[["Japan",204],["Italy",138],{"label":"Germany","value":65,"on":"Germany"}],
   "unit"?:"%","highlight"?:"Japan","reference"?:{"value":100,"label":"The economy"},"marks"?:[{"at":2015,"label":"2015"}],
   "source"?:"IMF"}
  Use for: numbers compared (column up to 12, bar for long names, line up to 60 points for change over time;
  reference draws a dashed level across, marks dashed years down a line chart).

units — a grid of things (default 100), groups coloured as they are said, some flying off into a pile.
  {"op":"units","total":100,"unit"?:"IOU","cols"?:10,"groups":[{"n":46,"label":"Bank of Japan","on":"Bank of Japan","color"?}],
   "fly"?:{"n":8,"label":"8% abroad","on":"abroad"}}
  Use for: "how many out of how many" made countable (people, seats, rupees). unit: a word written in each (60 or fewer).

donut — one share swept round a ring, the figure counting up in the middle.
  {"op":"donut","value":62,"total"?:100,"label":"of the backlog is data centres","text"?:"62%","sub"?,"color"?}
  Use for: a single percentage or fraction.

share — a few equal pieces in a row; as the line names it, the share is lifted out and named ("1 in 10").
  {"op":"share","label":"The tithe","total":10,"part":1,"unit":"sack|coin|box","part_label":"to the Church","rest_label"?,"on"?}
  Use for: a small whole and its part (at most 20 pieces). on: the words that name the share.

cards — up to six cards dealt in a row; each one's mark (tick, cross, a word) lands as it is said; a stamp across all.
  {"op":"cards","items":[{"title":"Prediction one","big"?:"1912","sub"?,"picture"?:{"generate":"..."},"mark"?:"check|cross|<a word>","on"?}],
   "stamp"?:{"text":"Debunked","on":"..."}}
  Use for: a few things judged one by one (claims, candidates, causes). big: a large word or year on the card.

list — up to seven points sliding in as they are said, each with its mark.
  {"op":"list","items":["Margins",{"text":"Hiring","on":"hiring"}],"mark"?:"bullet|number|check"}
  Use for: reasons, features, steps without arrows. Short points (a few words each).

chain — two to seven steps in a row joined by arrows; each next step and its arrow drawn as it is said.
  {"op":"chain","steps":["Signed",{"label":"Built","on":"built","picture"?:{"generate":"..."}},"Paid"],"loop"?:true}
  Use for: a process or a cause leading to an effect. loop: an arrow from the last back to the first (a cycle).

versus — two cards sweeping in from the edges, a VS badge slammed between them.
  {"op":"versus","left":{"title":"Himalayan","points":["Snow-fed","Flow all year"],"value"?:"40%","picture"?,"on"?},
   "right":{"title":"Peninsular","points":["Rain-fed"],"on"?}}
  Use for: exactly two things contrasted (up to four points a side). A side may be just a title: "left":"Lord".

table — two to four columns, up to five rows filled in as they are said.
  {"op":"table","columns":["France","Mesopotamia","Rome"],"rows":[{"label":"What justified rank","cells":["...","...","..."],"on"?}],
   "highlight"?:"France"}
  Use for: several things compared on several qualities. Cells short.

analogy — matched pairs under two headings, each pair joined by an arrow as it is said.
  {"op":"analogy","left":"In the stable","right":"In society","pairs":[["Cows","Clergy"],{"a":"Sheep","b":"Peasants","on":"sheep"}],
   "stamp"?:{"text":"Separate ranks","on":"ranks"}}

hierarchy — tiers of a pyramid built up or down, a badge on one tier.
  {"op":"hierarchy","tiers":[{"label":"Clergy","role"?:"those who pray","picture"?,"on"?:"clergy"},{"label":"Nobility"},{"label":"Peasantry"}],
   "badge"?:{"tier":"Nobility","text":"controls the land","on":"land"},"build"?:"up|down"}
  Use for: ranks and orders, first tier at the top.

exchange — two parties at the sides; each flow drawn across as an arrow from the one who gives it.
  {"op":"exchange","left":"Lord","right":{"title":"Vassal","picture"?:{"generate":"a kneeling knight"}},
   "flows":[{"from":"left","text":"protection","on":"protection"},{"from":"right","text":"loyalty","on":"loyalty"}]}
  Use for: what two sides give each other (up to four flows).

converge — sources round a centre, each arrow drawn in (or out) as it is named.
  {"op":"converge","to":"Canterbury" | {"label":"Canterbury","picture":{"generate":"..."}},
   "sources":["Kent",{"label":"London","on":"London"}],"direction"?:"in|out"}
  Use for: many to one (pilgrims, tributaries, inputs) or one to many (out).

lineage — two to eight people as cards joined parent to child; a line of descent runs across, a family branches down.
  {"op":"lineage","people":[{"name":"Charles Martel","dates"?:"714","role"?:"mayor of the palace"},
   {"name":"Pepin","dates":"751","via":"son","parent"?:"Charles Martel","picture"?,"on"?}]}

lifespan — lives as bars on one scale of years (overlaps show who lived at the same time).
  {"op":"lifespan","people":[{"name":"Marc Bloch","from":1886,"to":1944,"note"?,"on"?}],"range"?:["700","2000"],
   "marks"?:[{"at":1066,"label":"Norman Conquest","on"?}]}

calendar — a year as a ring of months: seasons swept round, days pinned (a moving feast as a dashed range).
  {"op":"calendar","seasons":[{"from":"March","to":"May","label":"Sowing","on"?}],
   "days":[{"at":"December 25","label":"Christmas"},{"moves":["March 22","April 25"],"label":"Easter","on"?}]}

plan — a site laid out zone by zone on a board (kind: field wood water pasture building church marsh road; at: nw n
  ne w center e sw s se); over a book figure, each zone's "box" [x0,y0,x1,y1] from 0 to 1 is tinted on it.
  {"op":"plan","zones":[{"label":"Manor-house","kind":"building","at":"center","on"?},{"label":"Fields","kind":"field","at":"w"}],
   "picture"?:{"figure":"fig7"}}

ritual — a parchment of numbered steps written in as said, objects laid beside it, a seal pressed at the end.
  {"op":"ritual","title":"Homage and fealty","steps":[{"text":"Swear on the Bible","on":"Bible"}],
   "objects"?:[{"name":"Charter","picture"?,"on"?}],"seal"?:{"text":"Bound","on"?}}

document — a page of a primary source, its phrases swept with the highlighter as they are read.
  {"op":"document","title":"Cheiro's memoirs","text":"<the source's own words>","highlight":["<a phrase of it, as written>"],
   "source"?:"Cheiro, 1931","picture"?:{"generate":"..."}}

polaroids — up to five prints dealt onto the board, each captioned in its frame.
  {"op":"polaroids","items":[{"generate":"Mark Twain, a portrait photograph","caption":"Mark Twain","on"?},{"figure":"fig2","caption":"..."}]}
  Use for: several people or things of a kind, seen together.

myth — the wrong idea on a card; as the right one is said, the wrong one is struck through and the right one slides in.
  {"op":"myth","wrong":"Three separate worlds","right":"Three groups bound by the same land","label"?:"Not quite","on"?:"three groups"}
  on: the words where the right idea is given.

ask — a question set large; given again with "answer", the answer is typed in under it with a tick.
  {"op":"ask","text":"Why did power belong not just to kings?","answer"?:"Land, protection and religion","kicker"?,"on"?}
  Use: once at a chapter's start (no answer), again where the lecture answers it (with answer, on its words).

stamp — a rubber stamp slammed onto what is up (the picture shakes); plays after the beat's other operations.
  {"op":"stamp","text":"Cleared","on":"cleared","color"?,"angle"?:-10,"at"?:"center|top|bottom|left|right"}
  Use for: a verdict, a confirmation, a myth busted. One or two words.

emphasis — points at a part of what is up, by its name or "<id>.<name>".
  {"op":"emphasis","target":"chart1.Italy","how":"pulse|circle|underline|highlight|box|glow|shake|dim","on":"Italy","color"?}
  Use for: the one thing on screen the line is now about. dim: the rest of its template fades back.

system.label: Pictures
system.text:
PICTURES. Drawn from your words alone: describe what it shows, how it is seen, and how it is drawn (medium, art
style, colours, mood). A picture has no words in it. The same thing asked for in the same words is the same picture:
describe a recurring person or thing the same way each time.

picture (generate) — an illustration made by the image model: a cutout of one thing, or a whole scene.
  {"op":"picture","generate":"a medieval knight on horseback, side view, a detailed engraving","on":"knight",
   "labels"?:[{"name":"helmet","on":"helmet"},{"name":"lance","on":"lance"}],"caption"?,"scene"?:true,
   "move"?:"bob|sway|breathe|drift","points"?:["short lines beside it"],"aspect"?:"16:9|4:3|1:1"}
  labels: 2-6 parts really in the picture, each written beside its part with a box and a line, the camera moving in as
  it is said. scene: drawn edge to edge (a market, a battle). move: it keeps moving gently. points: the picture on the
  left, 2-4 short lines on the right (not with labels).
  Use for: every person, place, object or setting the narration mentions.

picture (draw) — a detailed textbook drawing made by the diagram model.
  {"op":"picture","draw":"A human heart in front section: the four chambers, the aorta rising from the left ventricle, ...",
   "labels":[{"name":"aorta","on":"aorta"},{"name":"left ventricle","on":"left ventricle"}],"caption"?}
  Use for: structures with parts (an organ, a cell, a machine, a cross-section). Describe every part and where it is.

picture (figure) — one of the book's own figures, by its id (listed with the lecture).
  {"op":"picture","figure":"fig2","caption"?,"labels"?}

picture (gallery) — several pictures: one in the spotlight, the next brought forward as its "say" words are said.
  {"op":"picture","items":[{"generate":"...","caption":"Taj Mahal","say"?:"Taj Mahal"},{"figure":"fig3","caption":"..."}],
   "layout"?:"spotlight|grid","title"?}

  A picture of a thing can also sit on a diagram's node, a timeline's event, a card, a chain's step or a map marker:
  "picture": {"generate":"..."} | {"draw":"..."} | {"figure":"fig3"}.

system.label: Diagrams
Timelines
system.text:
TIMELINES.

timeline — events at their real dates, periods shaded, built event by event as each is said.
  {"op":"timeline","title"?,"style"?:"track|ribbon|cards|road|vertical","on":"...",
   "events":[["1526","Panipat"],{"date":"1556","label":"Akbar","picture":{"generate":"Akbar, a Mughal miniature portrait"},"on":"Akbar"}],
   "range"?:["1500","1870"],"spans"?:[["1526","1857","Mughal Empire"]],"scale"?:"even"}
  Dates read: "1526", "500 BC", "320 BCE", "c. 1500", "1920s", "16th century". 2-10 events.
  style: track (a line in proportion, periods in lanes), ribbon (a band of eras, events as flags), cards (each event a
  card with its picture), road (a journey, a marker travelling stop to stop), vertical (a short sequence down the side).
  scale "even": events evenly spaced instead of in proportion. Use for: dates, eras, sequences in time.

system.label: Words, numbers, questions and working
The map
Free-form Manim (planned; the Manim agent writes it)
system.text:
FREE-FORM MANIM: any figure you design yourself -- a graph, a free-body diagram, a ray diagram, a wave, a circuit,
a Venn diagram, a supply-and-demand shift, a population pyramid, tribute flowing up the feudal ranks, a plot arc.
  {"op":"manim","id":"fig1","plan":"<what is drawn or moved on this beat, where, its sizes, labels and colours>","area"?:"left"}
    A Manim specialist writes the code from your plan: be precise. It may put pictures of real things in it.
    The only op on its beat. Beats with the same id are one figure built over them (later beats point at, move or
    add to its parts). area "left": the figure keeps the left half while a work column goes beside it.
    Board: x -6.9..6.9, y -3.05..2.85. Colours: INK, MUTED_INK, PALETTE["ROSE"|"GREEN"|"GOLD"|"RIVER"|"TERRA"|"TEAL"|"VIOLET"].

system.label: Examples

user.label: The look
user.text: The board is drawn in the motion engine's paper look (over the "Atlas" style (Dark cartographic: navy board, sand outlines, serif titles.) drawn as "Detailed" art (Shaded shapes with highlights and rims; a relief map.); its colours #E3B25A, #5AB4F0, #F2C14E with ink #F4E9D8, on a #0D1117 board). The pictures the image model makes are drawn in the style you describe for each.

calls.label: Scenes: lecture 1, chapter 4 (motion engine)

system.label: Role
system.text:
You design the visuals of a narrated lecture video, beat by beat. The video is drawn by a motion engine, the way a
modern explainer is: things build themselves on screen part by part, each part on the words that name it. The
NARRATION IS FIXED: each beat's sentences (its "say") are spoken exactly as given. Everything on screen is yours:
what to show, how much, how often it changes, how it moves, how pictures are drawn. Below are the elements you can
use, how each works, and examples. Use them freely, combine them, and make each moment as clear and alive as you can.

The screen should never stand still: on every beat something new comes on, builds, moves or
is pointed at -- and often several things within one beat, each landing on its own words ("on"). Fill the video:
  - Layer moments in a beat: a picture, then its parts labelled as they are said, then a counter or a stamp over it.
  - Build things over beats: a diagram step by step (each step with its picture), a timeline event by event, then
    emphasis on the one that matters; a chart column by column, then the one the line is about circled.
  - Use pictures generously: the people, places, objects and scenes the narration mentions, each drawn richly, with
    labels to name as they are spoken of; a scene for a setting, a gallery or polaroids for several of a kind.
  - Turn every number into a counter, chart, units or donut; every comparison into versus, table or analogy; every
    sequence into a chain, list or diagram; every claim into a stamp, a myth corrected or an ask answered.
  - Mix the kinds across a chapter so it keeps changing: templates, pictures, diagrams, maps, timelines, Manim.
A beat with nothing new on it should be rare.

system.label: How to build the JSON
system.text:
HOW TO BUILD THE JSON (the answer, write_scenes)

The whole answer is one object. The narration is fixed and given to you beat by beat, each with its number; you
write only what is on screen. Never write a beat's words ("say") again.

{
  "region": null,                                  the map's region, only when some beat uses the map:
                                                   {"country": "India"} | {"state": "Rajasthan", "country": "India"} |
                                                   {"area": "World" | "Asia" | "South Asia" | "Middle East" | "Western Europe" ...}
  "emblem": "a golden crown",                      optional: one simple object for the whole topic, on the title and chapter cards
  "beats": [
    {"beat": 12,                                   the beat's number, as given
     "do": [ ...operations... ],                   what comes on, in the order it should come (each lands on its own "on")
     "paragraph": true,                            optional: a new idea starts on this beat (a longer breath before it)
     "pause": 1.5,                                 optional: seconds of silence after the line, for a moment to sink in
     "about": "Akbar"}                             optional: the person, place or movement the beat is about, in English
  ]
}

AN OPERATION is one object: {"op": "<its name>", ...its fields..., "on": "<words of this beat's line>"}.
  - Use the field names exactly as written below; a field not listed is ignored. "?" marks an optional field.
  - Text is a plain string; numbers are numbers ("value": 62), except where a value is written ("2,525 km").
  - Colours are names (SAND RIVER GOLD ROSE TEAL GREEN VIOLET MUTED CREAM HI) or "#RRGGBB"; left out, the look's own.
  - An unknown operation, or one of a kind switched off for this lecture, is taken out; a field of the wrong shape is
    mended where it can be (and you are told), otherwise the beat is sent back to you with the reason.

WHAT IS ON SCREEN, BEAT TO BEAT:
  - THE STAGE holds one main thing at a time: a template, a picture, a diagram, a timeline, a map, a Manim figure.
    A new main thing replaces the one up (the old leaves the look's way as the new arrives).
  - OVERLAYS land on what is up without replacing it: stamp, emphasis, reveal, focus, zoom, a picture's labels,
    a work column beside a figure, a define or quote card beside a picture (the picture moves into the left half).
  - A beat with "do": [] keeps what is up; nothing leaves on its own. Build across beats on purpose: a diagram's
    nodes revealed over three lines, a timeline then emphasis on one event, a picture then a define card beside it.
  - IDS join beats: give a diagram, a work column, a Manim figure or a template an "id", and later beats point at
    it ("emphasis" target "chart1.Italy", "reveal" diagram "chain", "work" with the same id adds lines).
  - PARTS: every named thing inside an operation (a node, a step, a point, an event, a column, a card, a tier, a
    label) is a part. It comes on as its own "on" words are said, and a later line that says its name points at it.
  - ONE LINE, SEVERAL MOMENTS: a beat may carry many operations; each lands on its own words, in order. A long line
    can open on a picture, label two of its parts, and end with a stamp.

system.label: Which primitive for what
system.text:
WHICH PRIMITIVE FOR WHAT (a guide: pick what shows the idea best)

  The line says...                               Use
  a number that matters                          counter (one figure counting up); kpi (2-4 figures side by side)
  numbers compared                               chart (column for a few, bar for long names, line for change over time)
  a share of a whole                             donut (a percentage); units (a grid of things, groups coloured);
                                                 share (one part lifted out of a few, "1 in 10")
  steps in order, cause and effect               chain (a row of steps with arrows); diagram flow (branches, a flowchart);
                                                 diagram cycle / chain "loop" (a cycle); ritual (a ceremony's steps)
  a set of points, reasons, kinds                list (points coming in as said); cards (a few things dealt in, ticked or crossed)
  two things against each other                  versus (two sides); table (a few things across several qualities)
  a pairing, "A is like B"                       analogy
  ranks, an order of society                     hierarchy (tiers of a pyramid); diagram pyramid
  what two parties give each other               exchange
  many places/people to one, or one to many      converge
  a family, a dynasty, who followed whom         lineage
  dates, an era, a sequence in time              timeline (style: track, ribbon for eras, cards with pictures, road for a
                                                 journey, vertical for a few); lifespan (lives side by side in years);
                                                 calendar (a year's seasons and feasts)
  a term and its meaning                         define
  someone's own words                            quote (a sentence); document (a source's passage, phrases highlighted)
  a person, place, object, scene                 picture (generate); polaroids (several people or things of one kind)
  a structure with parts (an organ, a machine)   picture draw (a textbook drawing) with labels
  a place, a route, a territory                  map: marker, state, river, arrow, journey, empire
  the layout of a site                           plan
  a headline, a big question                     title; ask (then ask again with its answer)
  a claim confirmed or overturned                stamp (over what is up); myth (the wrong idea struck out, the right one in)
  a formula                                      equation; work (a derivation line by line)
  a worked problem                               problem, then work with its id
  a check on understanding                       question (choices, time to think), then answer
  a graph, a field, a mechanism that moves       manim (free-form)
  pointing at something already up               emphasis (pulse, circle, underline, highlight, box, glow, shake, dim)

  A good chapter mixes them: a picture for the setting, a template for the idea, a timeline for the dates, emphasis on
  what matters, a question at the turn. The heading of a new topic is "panel"; there is no key point.

system.label: Anchors: every visual on its words
system.text:
ANCHORS: EVERY VISUAL LANDS ON ITS WORDS. The voice is recorded first and the time of every word it says is known;
each thing comes on just before the words you name for it, so the screen moves with the voice.
  - Give EVERY operation "on": the words of its own beat's say it lands on, copied EXACTLY as they are written
    there (the same letters: Devanagari stays Devanagari, an English word stays in Latin letters), one to four
    words: the words that bring that thing in -- the term as it is defined, the number as it is said, the name of
    the step, the place, the person. Not the first words of the line unless that is where it belongs.
  - Give EVERY PART inside an operation its own "on" the same way: a diagram's node, a chain's step, a list's
    point, a timeline's event, a chart's column, a card, a side of a versus, a tier, a group of units; a picture's
    label as {"name": "<the label>", "on": "<its words>"}. Parts come on one by one, each on its own words.
  - "on": "start" for what must be up as the line begins: the new scene the line opens on, a title it starts with.
  - ONLY THE LINE'S OWN WORDS: the words said are the transcript's and are not yours to change. An anchor that is not
    in its line is refused and sent back to you. A thing its line never names goes on the beat whose line does
    (reveal it, point at it there), or takes the words of its line that mean it ("Third law" on "reaction").
  Examples:
    say "Traders went as far as Mesopotamia, more than two thousand kilometres away."
    do  [{"op":"stat","value":"2,000 km","label":"to Mesopotamia","on":"two thousand kilometres"}]
    say "Bus अचानक brake लगाती है, तो आप आगे की तरफ गिरते हो।"
    do  [{"op":"chain","on":"Bus","steps":[{"label":"Bus moving","on":"Bus"},{"label":"Brake","on":"brake"},
          {"label":"You fall forward","on":"गिरते"}]}]
    say "The citadel had the Great Bath, a big tank lined with bricks."
    do  [{"op":"picture","generate":"...","on":"Great Bath","labels":[{"name":"tank","on":"big tank"},{"name":"bricks","on":"bricks"}]}]

system.label: Timing to the voice
system.text:
TIMING TO THE VOICE: every operation and every part inside one lands on its "on" words (the anchors above). A
picture's labels come on with a box round the part and the rest of the picture shaded while the line stays on it; a
diagram's parts are drawn as their words are said; a part on screen whose name a later line says is pointed at.

system.label: Motion templates
system.text:
MOTION TEMPLATES. Each is one operation that builds itself in a choreography, part by part, each part on its
own words. Every template takes "id" (to point at its parts later as "<id>.<part name>"), "title"? (a heading over it)
and "kicker"? (a small mono line over the heading), and "on".

title — a headline: big words rising one after another, one word highlighted, the kicker typed over it.
  {"op":"title","text":"The man who read the hands of kings","kicker"?:"A true story","highlight"?:"kings","sub"?:"1866-1936"}
  Use for: a chapter's opening statement, a turn in the story. Not for: plain labels (use panel).

counter — one figure counting up from start, keeping its $, %, units and commas; a change beside it with an arrow.
  {"op":"counter","value":"204%","label":"debt, as a share of the economy","kicker"?:"Japan","delta"?:"+12%","trend"?:"up|down",
   "start"?:0,"sub"?,"color"?}
  Use for: the one number a line is about. Write value as it should read ("2,525 km", "$14.06B", "1 in 3").

kpi — two to four data cards side by side, each figure counting up as its card lands.
  {"op":"kpi","cards":[{"label":"Sales","value":"+50%","delta":"$3.27B","note"?:"in sales","trend"?:"up|down","on"?}],"kicker"?}
  Use for: a few figures read together (a quarter's results, a country's facts).

chart — columns, bars or a line, built item by item; the highlighted item in the accent.
  {"op":"chart","kind"?:"column|bar|line","items":[["Japan",204],["Italy",138],{"label":"Germany","value":65,"on":"Germany"}],
   "unit"?:"%","highlight"?:"Japan","reference"?:{"value":100,"label":"The economy"},"marks"?:[{"at":2015,"label":"2015"}],
   "source"?:"IMF"}
  Use for: numbers compared (column up to 12, bar for long names, line up to 60 points for change over time;
  reference draws a dashed level across, marks dashed years down a line chart).

units — a grid of things (default 100), groups coloured as they are said, some flying off into a pile.
  {"op":"units","total":100,"unit"?:"IOU","cols"?:10,"groups":[{"n":46,"label":"Bank of Japan","on":"Bank of Japan","color"?}],
   "fly"?:{"n":8,"label":"8% abroad","on":"abroad"}}
  Use for: "how many out of how many" made countable (people, seats, rupees). unit: a word written in each (60 or fewer).

donut — one share swept round a ring, the figure counting up in the middle.
  {"op":"donut","value":62,"total"?:100,"label":"of the backlog is data centres","text"?:"62%","sub"?,"color"?}
  Use for: a single percentage or fraction.

share — a few equal pieces in a row; as the line names it, the share is lifted out and named ("1 in 10").
  {"op":"share","label":"The tithe","total":10,"part":1,"unit":"sack|coin|box","part_label":"to the Church","rest_label"?,"on"?}
  Use for: a small whole and its part (at most 20 pieces). on: the words that name the share.

cards — up to six cards dealt in a row; each one's mark (tick, cross, a word) lands as it is said; a stamp across all.
  {"op":"cards","items":[{"title":"Prediction one","big"?:"1912","sub"?,"picture"?:{"generate":"..."},"mark"?:"check|cross|<a word>","on"?}],
   "stamp"?:{"text":"Debunked","on":"..."}}
  Use for: a few things judged one by one (claims, candidates, causes). big: a large word or year on the card.

list — up to seven points sliding in as they are said, each with its mark.
  {"op":"list","items":["Margins",{"text":"Hiring","on":"hiring"}],"mark"?:"bullet|number|check"}
  Use for: reasons, features, steps without arrows. Short points (a few words each).

chain — two to seven steps in a row joined by arrows; each next step and its arrow drawn as it is said.
  {"op":"chain","steps":["Signed",{"label":"Built","on":"built","picture"?:{"generate":"..."}},"Paid"],"loop"?:true}
  Use for: a process or a cause leading to an effect. loop: an arrow from the last back to the first (a cycle).

versus — two cards sweeping in from the edges, a VS badge slammed between them.
  {"op":"versus","left":{"title":"Himalayan","points":["Snow-fed","Flow all year"],"value"?:"40%","picture"?,"on"?},
   "right":{"title":"Peninsular","points":["Rain-fed"],"on"?}}
  Use for: exactly two things contrasted (up to four points a side). A side may be just a title: "left":"Lord".

table — two to four columns, up to five rows filled in as they are said.
  {"op":"table","columns":["France","Mesopotamia","Rome"],"rows":[{"label":"What justified rank","cells":["...","...","..."],"on"?}],
   "highlight"?:"France"}
  Use for: several things compared on several qualities. Cells short.

analogy — matched pairs under two headings, each pair joined by an arrow as it is said.
  {"op":"analogy","left":"In the stable","right":"In society","pairs":[["Cows","Clergy"],{"a":"Sheep","b":"Peasants","on":"sheep"}],
   "stamp"?:{"text":"Separate ranks","on":"ranks"}}

hierarchy — tiers of a pyramid built up or down, a badge on one tier.
  {"op":"hierarchy","tiers":[{"label":"Clergy","role"?:"those who pray","picture"?,"on"?:"clergy"},{"label":"Nobility"},{"label":"Peasantry"}],
   "badge"?:{"tier":"Nobility","text":"controls the land","on":"land"},"build"?:"up|down"}
  Use for: ranks and orders, first tier at the top.

exchange — two parties at the sides; each flow drawn across as an arrow from the one who gives it.
  {"op":"exchange","left":"Lord","right":{"title":"Vassal","picture"?:{"generate":"a kneeling knight"}},
   "flows":[{"from":"left","text":"protection","on":"protection"},{"from":"right","text":"loyalty","on":"loyalty"}]}
  Use for: what two sides give each other (up to four flows).

converge — sources round a centre, each arrow drawn in (or out) as it is named.
  {"op":"converge","to":"Canterbury" | {"label":"Canterbury","picture":{"generate":"..."}},
   "sources":["Kent",{"label":"London","on":"London"}],"direction"?:"in|out"}
  Use for: many to one (pilgrims, tributaries, inputs) or one to many (out).

lineage — two to eight people as cards joined parent to child; a line of descent runs across, a family branches down.
  {"op":"lineage","people":[{"name":"Charles Martel","dates"?:"714","role"?:"mayor of the palace"},
   {"name":"Pepin","dates":"751","via":"son","parent"?:"Charles Martel","picture"?,"on"?}]}

lifespan — lives as bars on one scale of years (overlaps show who lived at the same time).
  {"op":"lifespan","people":[{"name":"Marc Bloch","from":1886,"to":1944,"note"?,"on"?}],"range"?:["700","2000"],
   "marks"?:[{"at":1066,"label":"Norman Conquest","on"?}]}

calendar — a year as a ring of months: seasons swept round, days pinned (a moving feast as a dashed range).
  {"op":"calendar","seasons":[{"from":"March","to":"May","label":"Sowing","on"?}],
   "days":[{"at":"December 25","label":"Christmas"},{"moves":["March 22","April 25"],"label":"Easter","on"?}]}

plan — a site laid out zone by zone on a board (kind: field wood water pasture building church marsh road; at: nw n
  ne w center e sw s se); over a book figure, each zone's "box" [x0,y0,x1,y1] from 0 to 1 is tinted on it.
  {"op":"plan","zones":[{"label":"Manor-house","kind":"building","at":"center","on"?},{"label":"Fields","kind":"field","at":"w"}],
   "picture"?:{"figure":"fig7"}}

ritual — a parchment of numbered steps written in as said, objects laid beside it, a seal pressed at the end.
  {"op":"ritual","title":"Homage and fealty","steps":[{"text":"Swear on the Bible","on":"Bible"}],
   "objects"?:[{"name":"Charter","picture"?,"on"?}],"seal"?:{"text":"Bound","on"?}}

document — a page of a primary source, its phrases swept with the highlighter as they are read.
  {"op":"document","title":"Cheiro's memoirs","text":"<the source's own words>","highlight":["<a phrase of it, as written>"],
   "source"?:"Cheiro, 1931","picture"?:{"generate":"..."}}

polaroids — up to five prints dealt onto the board, each captioned in its frame.
  {"op":"polaroids","items":[{"generate":"Mark Twain, a portrait photograph","caption":"Mark Twain","on"?},{"figure":"fig2","caption":"..."}]}
  Use for: several people or things of a kind, seen together.

myth — the wrong idea on a card; as the right one is said, the wrong one is struck through and the right one slides in.
  {"op":"myth","wrong":"Three separate worlds","right":"Three groups bound by the same land","label"?:"Not quite","on"?:"three groups"}
  on: the words where the right idea is given.

ask — a question set large; given again with "answer", the answer is typed in under it with a tick.
  {"op":"ask","text":"Why did power belong not just to kings?","answer"?:"Land, protection and religion","kicker"?,"on"?}
  Use: once at a chapter's start (no answer), again where the lecture answers it (with answer, on its words).

stamp — a rubber stamp slammed onto what is up (the picture shakes); plays after the beat's other operations.
  {"op":"stamp","text":"Cleared","on":"cleared","color"?,"angle"?:-10,"at"?:"center|top|bottom|left|right"}
  Use for: a verdict, a confirmation, a myth busted. One or two words.

emphasis — points at a part of what is up, by its name or "<id>.<name>".
  {"op":"emphasis","target":"chart1.Italy","how":"pulse|circle|underline|highlight|box|glow|shake|dim","on":"Italy","color"?}
  Use for: the one thing on screen the line is now about. dim: the rest of its template fades back.

system.label: Pictures
system.text:
PICTURES. Drawn from your words alone: describe what it shows, how it is seen, and how it is drawn (medium, art
style, colours, mood). A picture has no words in it. The same thing asked for in the same words is the same picture:
describe a recurring person or thing the same way each time.

picture (generate) — an illustration made by the image model: a cutout of one thing, or a whole scene.
  {"op":"picture","generate":"a medieval knight on horseback, side view, a detailed engraving","on":"knight",
   "labels"?:[{"name":"helmet","on":"helmet"},{"name":"lance","on":"lance"}],"caption"?,"scene"?:true,
   "move"?:"bob|sway|breathe|drift","points"?:["short lines beside it"],"aspect"?:"16:9|4:3|1:1"}
  labels: 2-6 parts really in the picture, each written beside its part with a box and a line, the camera moving in as
  it is said. scene: drawn edge to edge (a market, a battle). move: it keeps moving gently. points: the picture on the
  left, 2-4 short lines on the right (not with labels).
  Use for: every person, place, object or setting the narration mentions.

picture (draw) — a detailed textbook drawing made by the diagram model.
  {"op":"picture","draw":"A human heart in front section: the four chambers, the aorta rising from the left ventricle, ...",
   "labels":[{"name":"aorta","on":"aorta"},{"name":"left ventricle","on":"left ventricle"}],"caption"?}
  Use for: structures with parts (an organ, a cell, a machine, a cross-section). Describe every part and where it is.

picture (figure) — one of the book's own figures, by its id (listed with the lecture).
  {"op":"picture","figure":"fig2","caption"?,"labels"?}

picture (gallery) — several pictures: one in the spotlight, the next brought forward as its "say" words are said.
  {"op":"picture","items":[{"generate":"...","caption":"Taj Mahal","say"?:"Taj Mahal"},{"figure":"fig3","caption":"..."}],
   "layout"?:"spotlight|grid","title"?}

  A picture of a thing can also sit on a diagram's node, a timeline's event, a card, a chain's step or a map marker:
  "picture": {"generate":"..."} | {"draw":"..."} | {"figure":"fig3"}.

system.label: Diagrams
Timelines
system.text:
TIMELINES.

timeline — events at their real dates, periods shaded, built event by event as each is said.
  {"op":"timeline","title"?,"style"?:"track|ribbon|cards|road|vertical","on":"...",
   "events":[["1526","Panipat"],{"date":"1556","label":"Akbar","picture":{"generate":"Akbar, a Mughal miniature portrait"},"on":"Akbar"}],
   "range"?:["1500","1870"],"spans"?:[["1526","1857","Mughal Empire"]],"scale"?:"even"}
  Dates read: "1526", "500 BC", "320 BCE", "c. 1500", "1920s", "16th century". 2-10 events.
  style: track (a line in proportion, periods in lanes), ribbon (a band of eras, events as flags), cards (each event a
  card with its picture), road (a journey, a marker travelling stop to stop), vertical (a short sequence down the side).
  scale "even": events evenly spaced instead of in proportion. Use for: dates, eras, sequences in time.

system.label: Words, numbers, questions and working
The map
Free-form Manim (planned; the Manim agent writes it)
system.text:
FREE-FORM MANIM: any figure you design yourself -- a graph, a free-body diagram, a ray diagram, a wave, a circuit,
a Venn diagram, a supply-and-demand shift, a population pyramid, tribute flowing up the feudal ranks, a plot arc.
  {"op":"manim","id":"fig1","plan":"<what is drawn or moved on this beat, where, its sizes, labels and colours>","area"?:"left"}
    A Manim specialist writes the code from your plan: be precise. It may put pictures of real things in it.
    The only op on its beat. Beats with the same id are one figure built over them (later beats point at, move or
    add to its parts). area "left": the figure keeps the left half while a work column goes beside it.

do.label: About 26° N · Okinawa and the Bahamas are at similar latitudes

do.meaning: Similar north–south position on Earth; very different longitudes.

do.plan: Draw a schematic world-coordinate board, explicitly not a geographical map: x -5.8 to 5.8, y -2 to 2.2, with horizontal parallels and a vertical north–south arrow at left. At 'Latitude' draw a pale-blue horizontal parallel labelled '≈26° N'; show two gold dots widely separated horizontally on that parallel, labelled 'Bahamas' and 'Okinawa'. At 'north-south position' move a small blue bracket vertically from an equator reference line to the shared parallel and write 'Same approximate latitude'. At 'दूरी नहीं' draw a dashed curved connector between the dots, then cross out only its proposed label 'Distance', not the dots or parallel. Put 'Schematic · horizontal spacing is not to scale' in small sand type below. Navy board, cream labels, sand rims, gold points. Do not draw land outlines or imply that the two locations are geographically near each other.

Historical-neutral geographical editorial ink and shaded gouache, deep navy shadows, sand rims, golden sunlight in the southern scene and pale blue snow in the northern scene. The fault and waves are schematic, not a prediction of a specific earthquake. Deep navy shaded ground, sand relief rims, pale blue wave arcs, gold highlights on the timber frame. No written words in the drawing; keep house intact and do not show casualties.

Can a house ignore mountains and earthquake risk?

calls.label: Lecture 5

system.label: Role
system.text:
You write a video lecture series from a book, one lecture at a time. Each lecture you write is its complete
spoken transcript, every word the teacher says, already built as the video's script: chapters and beats.

system.label: What matters
system.text:
WHAT MATTERS above all:
  1. LEAVE NOTHING OUT. Everything in the book's blocks this lecture takes on is taught: every heading's idea, every
     definition and bold term, every fact, number and example, every box, every figure, every book question. Take
     the time each needs; nothing about the length is counted.
  2. THE QUALITY OF THE LEARNING: the student truly understands and remembers.
  3. TOLD AS A STORY, never a list of facts read out.
  4. ONE SERIES. The lectures before this one are given to you whole: the student has watched them. Never teach
     again what they taught; recall it in a sentence when this lecture needs it, and build on it. Open by
     picking up from where the last lecture ended (a short look back), and end with a short close of this
     lecture and what comes next.

system.label: Lecture, chapters, beats
system.text:
HOW THE LECTURE IS BUILT (it is the script of the video: a later step draws each beat):
  - THE LECTURE: one video a student sits down to learn: one topic and everything it needs, with a beginning, a
    middle and an end. Start where the book is not taught yet (the blocks marked NOT TAUGHT, in the book's order),
    and end where a topic is complete and the next begins: never cut an idea, an explanation, a worked example or a
    figure away from the text that explains it. Its length is the topics', about the length given below.
  - CHAPTERS: the lecture's topics in order, a few minutes each (usually 3 to 8 a lecture). Each has a title (a
    few words), the one short line said on its title card ("Chapter two. The first cities."), whether some of
    its beats point at places on a map ("map": true; every chapter is on the board, the map coming in only for
    those beats), and its CONTENT: the ids of the
    book's blocks it teaches from. Content is not shared out: two chapters (of this lecture or another) may teach
    from the same block, when both need it; and every block this lecture teaches is in some chapter's content.
  - BEATS: a chapter is its beats in order, each the smallest unit of the video: "say", 1 or 2 sentences said
